## China Market Entry: Test Before You Commit
Source: https://www.goods-infinite.com/insights/china-market-entry-test-before-commit
Published: 2026-10-28 · Cluster: Market Entry & Entity

## What a China market entry pilot actually is

**A China market entry pilot is a bounded, reversible commercial test in which a foreign brand sells real product to real Chinese buyers through channels that do not require a registered local entity, used to convert market-entry risk into numbers before committing capital to registration, offices or inventory depth.** It sits between two things it must not be confused with. Market research produces estimates; a pilot produces transactions. A full launch produces commitments; a pilot is designed to be abandoned. The discipline is in the boundaries: each rung has a spend cap, a legal perimeter and a decision date written down before the first order ships. Brands that skip the definition drift from research straight to a flagship store, and absorb the cost of both without the evidence of either.

## Why pilot-first is now the default for foreign brands

**Pilot-first entry has become the default because the registration climate opened faster than the demand climate, making commitment the scarce resource.** China's 2024 negative list removed the last manufacturing restrictions for foreign investors, leaving fewer than thirty restricted categories ([State Council NDRC-MOFCOM Order, 2024 negative list](https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/202409/content_6973149.htm)). Legally, almost nothing stops a foreign brand from going all-in. Commercially, the crowd data says otherwise: 70,392 new foreign-invested enterprises registered in China in 2025, up 19.1 percent, while actually used foreign investment fell 9.5 percent in the same year. More entrants, smaller tickets — the market itself is voting for staged commitment, and a pilot is what staged commitment looks like on paper.

<div class="statcard"><span class="n">70,392</span><span class="l">New foreign-invested enterprises set up in China in 2025, up 19.1 percent year on year — while actually used foreign investment fell 9.5 percent: more entrants, smaller tickets</span><span class="src">Source: MOFCOM 2025 full-year FDI statistics</span></div>

## The legal line: what cross-border retail lets a pilot skip

**The cross-border retail import policy is the legal foundation of a pilot, because it waives the one cost that makes testing expensive: product registration.** Under the framework notice governing cross-border e-commerce retail imports, goods bought through bonded (1210) or direct-purchase (9610) channels are supervised as personal-use items and are not subject to the first-import licence, registration or filing requirements that general trade imposes ([MOFCOM and four ministries, Shang Cai Fa 486 of 2018](https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2018-12/31/content_5437823.htm)). The waiver has obligations attached. Sellers must publish a risk notice where shoppers order, and must give consumers access to a Chinese electronic label, because a cross-border product may lawfully lack a printed Chinese label. The line is the channel, not the product: the same SKU sold offline through general trade crosses back into full registration the day it clears customs that way.

## The 1210 bonded pilot: the definitive test

**A 1210 bonded pilot is the strongest single test in the ladder because it puts sellable inventory inside a Chinese free-trade-zone warehouse without paying import duty on units that never sell.** Stock one pallet of your product with a bonded operator, open a cross-border storefront, and sell for a full season. Tax is charged per order as units are released: within the RMB 5,000 per-order and RMB 26,000 per-buyer-per-year quotas, tariff is zero and value-added and consumption taxes are levied at 70 percent of the domestic rate ([MOF, Cai Guan Shui 49 of 2018](https://gss.mof.gov.cn/gzdt/zhengcefabu/201811/t20181129_3079073.htm)). Two clocks frame the risk. Bonded storage runs one year from entry, extendable in most cases by one further year ([GACC Order No. 105, consolidated text](https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/2018-05/29/content_5723452.htm)), and unsellable stock has a defined destruction route with a 60-day completion window once triggered. The quota ceilings also shape the test design: they cap how much one customer can absorb, so the pilot should sample breadth of buyers rather than depth per buyer.

<div class="statcard"><span class="n">RMB 26,000</span><span class="l">Annual per-buyer ceiling for cross-border retail imports, with RMB 5,000 per single order — caps how far any one customer can pull your category and forces pilots to measure buyer breadth, not basket depth</span><span class="src">Source: Cai Guan Shui [2018] No. 49, effective 1 January 2019</span></div>

## Distributor pilots: territory by trial

**A distributor pilot is a general-trade test in miniature: one province, one season, a minimum-volume clause and a written exit, used to measure offline demand that cross-border channels structurally cannot see.** The negotiating position is everything. Agree a single-city or single-province territory rather than national exclusivity, set minimum purchase volumes the distributor partly funds, and date-stamp the exit clause before the first purchase order. Vet the counterpart before the contract, not after the first dispute: registration records, customs credit status and litigation history are all public ([see our distributor due-diligence checklist](https://www.goods-infinite.com/insights/vet-china-distributor-due-diligence.html)). A distributor trial tests two things at once — the region's demand and the partner's execution — and the pilot framing keeps both reversible: if the province disappoints, the clause expires without a market exit.

## The commitment ladder compared

**The commitment ladder is the sequencing rule that keeps each test cheap enough to abandon and each graduation earned by evidence.** Costs below are the fixed, non-refundable parts, not the total spend.

<div class="table-wrap"><table><thead><tr><th>Rung</th><th>Cash at risk</th><th>Legal boundary</th><th>Graduation signal</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>Demand test (no stock)</td><td>Research and ad spend only</td><td>None — no goods cross the border</td><td>Search and category data clear your threshold</td></tr>
<tr><td>1210 bonded pilot</td><td>One pallet of inventory + bonded and platform setup</td><td>Personal-use supervision; no first-import registration</td><td>Season sell-through and repeat rate hit plan</td></tr>
<tr><td>Distributor trial</td><td>Working capital + vetting</td><td>Full general-trade rules apply to the goods</td><td>Minimum volumes met without subsidy</td></tr>
<tr><td>Cross-border flagship</td><td>Store deposit + annual fee</td><td>Cross-border policy still applies</td><td>Stable unit economics across two seasons</td></tr>
<tr><td>General trade + local structure</td><td>Registration, IOR, entity costs</td><td>Category registration, labelling, IOR of record</td><td>—</td></tr></tbody></table></div>

The flagship rung carries real fixed costs — a Tmall Global store requires a RMB 50,000 deposit and an annual fee of RMB 30,000 to 60,000 depending on category, before commission — which is precisely why it belongs above the pallet, not below it.

## Graduation triggers: when the pilot has done its job

**A graduation trigger is a pre-agreed evidence threshold that converts a pilot into a launch decision, and writing the triggers down before the pilot starts is what separates a test from procrastination.** Four signals matter most. First, sell-through: a full season that clears the pallet at viable pricing without unplanned discounting. Second, repeat purchase: when loyal buyers start brushing the RMB 26,000 annual cross-border ceiling, the channel itself is telling you it has a per-customer lid. Third, channel demand: buyers, gifting occasions or retail buyers asking for offline availability that bonded fulfilment cannot serve. Fourth, margin: when volume makes category registration and general-trade duty cheaper per unit than the cross-border route — for a 13 percent value-added-tax goods line, cross-border effective tax is about 9.1 percent, but general trade wins once scale and offline pricing enter. Any two triggers together justify graduating.

## What a bonded pilot cannot tell you

**A bonded pilot samples the cross-border shopper, and that sample is skewed in ways a graduation decision must correct for.** China's cross-border retail imports are consumer goods end to end: in 2025 the channel took in RMB 570.2 billion, up 2.7 percent, with beauty and personal care at 27.2 percent and food and fresh goods at 23.9 percent of imports ([GACC 2025 cross-border e-commerce statistics](http://www.customs.gov.cn/tjs/2026-06/16/article_2026061616113844507.html)). Destinations cluster: Guangdong, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Shanghai and Shandong together took 44.3 percent of the value. A pilot therefore proves demand among digitised, import-minded consumers in wealthier coastal provinces. It cannot prove anything about lower-tier offline demand, where your category may live or die. That gap is why the ladder pairs channels instead of picking one: the bonded pallet answers product-market fit, the distributor trial answers geography.

## Supplements in China: 'Blue Hat' Health Food vs General Food — Which Route Does Your Product Take?
Source: https://www.goods-infinite.com/insights/supplements-blue-hat-vs-general-food
Published: 2026-10-28 · Cluster: Compliance & Registration

## China has no legal category called "supplement" — and that single fact decides your entire launch

Ask a Chinese regulator what a "supplement" is and you will get three different answers depending on which desk you ask. In Chinese law the word does not exist as a product category. What exists is a classification exercise: a bottle of vitamins, a fish-oil softgel and a collagen sachet each fall into one of three legal identities, and each identity comes with its own approval clock, its own claim ceiling and its own distribution rights. Get the classification right before you commission artwork and you can be selling in weeks. Get it wrong and the most common outcome is not a fine — it is a two-year pause while a registration dossier works its way through technical review, or a listing that gets pulled the week after launch because the copy implied a function the product is not approved to claim.

This guide sets out the decision tree, the statutory hooks behind each branch, and the numbers that actually drive the timeline.

<div class="statcard"><span class="n">24 + 24 + 10</span><span class="l">The complete claim ceiling: 24 permitted non-nutrient health functions (2023 catalogue), 24 nutrients plus n-3 in the nutrient-supplement catalogue, and 10 non-nutrient ingredients admitted to the health food raw material directory</span><span class="src">Source: SAMR / NHC / NATCM, Allowed Health Food Function Claim Catalogue — Non-Nutrient Supplements (2023 Edition), 15 August 2023; SAMR reply Guo Shi Jian Ti [2026] No. 243</span></div>

## The three legal identities a foreign supplement can take in China

Everything downstream follows from this table. Read it as a decision made per SKU, not per brand — a range of five products routinely splits across two or three rows.

<div class="table-wrap"><table>
<thead><tr><th></th><th>Health food (保健食品)</th><th>Ordinary food (普通食品)</th><th>Cross-border retail import</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td><strong>Legal basis</strong></td><td>Food Safety Law Arts. 74–79; Health Food Registration and Filing Measures</td><td>Food Safety Law general provisions; Implementation Regulation Art. 38</td><td>Shang Cai Fa [2018] No. 486, Section 3</td></tr>
<tr><td><strong>Pre-market approval</strong></td><td>Registration (注册) or filing (备案), then blue-hat mark and approval number</td><td>No health approval; standard import food requirements apply</td><td>Exempt from first-import licence, registration and filing</td></tr>
<tr><td><strong>Health claims</strong></td><td>Yes — only from the closed catalogue</td><td><strong>None.</strong> Implementation Regulation Art. 38 prohibits health-function claims on non-health foods</td><td>None beyond what Chinese advertising and food law permits for the copy</td></tr>

</tbody>
</table></div>

Which row you land on is decided by two questions: does your ingredient appear on the official raw material directory, and do you need to claim a function at all?

## Ordinary food is the fastest route and the one that forbids the most

There is a widespread assumption among foreign supplement brands that entering as ordinary food is a loophole. It is not — it is a legally valid route that simply comes with a gag order attached.

Art. 38 of the <a href="https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/content/2019-10/31/content_5447142.htm" rel="nofollow">Regulation on the Implementation of the Food Safety Law</a> (State Council Order No. 721, in force 1 December 2019) is one sentence long and does all the work: **for foods other than health food, no claim of a health function may be made.** Art. 39 then requires sellers to check that the label and instructions match the registered or filed version before selling, and prohibits displaying special foods mixed with ordinary food or with drugs.

In practice this means a product that enters as ordinary food can be imported, bonded, listed and sold — but the words "immune", "sleep", "joint", "liver", "blood sugar" and their softer cousins ("supports", "helps maintain", "clinically studied") all have to come off the label, the detail page and the livestream script. Most enforcement actions in this category are claim actions, not import actions: the goods cleared customs perfectly well and were then sold with copy that the product's legal identity does not permit.

<div class="statcard"><span class="n">14,000+ / 26,000+</span><span class="l">Valid health food registration certificates and cumulative health food filing certificates issued by SAMR — the two-track system is mature, not experimental</span><span class="src">Source: SAMR reply to NPC deputy suggestion No. 5496 (Guo Shi Jian Ti [2026]), figures as of end-May / end-June 2026</span></div>

## Health food: the blue hat, and the two routes that get you one

Health food (保健食品) is a statutory special-food category — defined in GB 16740 as food that claims and has a specific health function, or that is intended to supplement vitamins and minerals, is suitable for a defined population, regulates body function, is not intended to treat disease, and produces no acute, sub-acute or chronic harm. Approved products carry the blue hat-shaped mark plus an approval number. Only those products may make a health function claim.

The <a href="https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/2020-11/03/content_5723694.htm" rel="nofollow">Measures for the Administration of Health Food Registration and Filing</a> (published as CFDA Order No. 22, revised by SAMR Order No. 31, in force 23 October 2020) split the route in two.

### Filing (备案): directory ingredients, on-the-spot completion

Art. 9 requires registration for products using an ingredient **outside** the health food raw material directory, and for **first-import** health foods — with one carve-out: a first-import health food that is a vitamin/mineral nutrient supplement is filed instead of registered. Art. 5 assigns the filing of first-import nutrient supplements to SAMR itself, and other filings to the provincial market regulator. Art. 50 states that where the filing materials are satisfactory, filing is completed **on the spot**, and Art. 51 sets the numbering format 食健备G (domestic) / 食健备J (imported).

The current directory, per SAMR's own 2026 reply, covers **24 nutrients corresponding to 85 compound sources** and **10 non-nutrient ingredients** (ginseng, American ginseng, lingzhi and others). A parallel SAMR paper on marine health food confirms that ten functional ingredients including fish oil and spirulina have been brought into the filing directory.

### Registration (注册): substantive review, and the clock is longer than it looks

<div class="table-wrap"><table>
<thead><tr><th>Step</th><th>Statutory clock</th><th>Article</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td>Technical review by the evaluation body</td><td>60 working days, extendable by 20</td><td>Art. 16</td></tr>
<tr><td>Applicant supplements materials after a single consolidated notice</td><td>3 months to respond; <strong>review clock restarts</strong></td><td>Art. 19</td></tr>
<tr><td>On-site verification</td><td>30 working days</td><td>Art. 20</td></tr>
<tr><td>Re-test by the verification laboratory</td><td>60 working days</td><td>Art. 21</td></tr>
<tr><td>Request for re-review after a proposed refusal</td><td>20 working days to request; 30 working days to decide</td><td>Art. 24</td></tr>
<tr><td>SAMR decision after acceptance</td><td>20 working days</td><td>Art. 26</td></tr>
<tr><td>Issue of certificate or refusal</td><td>10 working days</td><td>Art. 28</td></tr>
<tr><td>Certificate validity</td><td>5 years; renewal applied for 6 months before expiry</td><td>Arts. 42, 32</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table></div>

Art. 27 is the one that catches people: **on-site verification, re-testing and re-review time are not counted** in the review or decision periods. So the statutory 20 working days at SAMR sits on top of a technical review that can run 80 working days and restart.

Two further points decide whether you can file at all.

**Who may apply.** Art. 11: the applicant for an imported health food registration must be the **overseas manufacturer** that markets the product, and the application must be handled through its resident representative office in China or a **commissioned Chinese agency**. A foreign trading company that does not manufacture cannot be the applicant.

**The origin-market gate.** Art. 13 requires, for a first-import registration, proof that the product **has been marketed for more than one year** in the country of origin, or a safety report covering overseas sales and human consumption; the relevant technical regulations or standards of that country; and actual samples of the overseas package, label and instructions. Alongside this, Art. 76 of the <a href="https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/2015-04/25/content_2853643.htm" rel="nofollow">Food Safety Law</a> requires that an imported health food be a product permitted to be marketed by the competent authority of the exporting country or region. A brand-new SKU launched only in the home market last quarter cannot be registered in China next quarter.

## What you are allowed to say: the closed catalogue

On 15 August 2023, SAMR together with the National Health Commission and the National Administration of Traditional Chinese Medicine published the <a href="https://www.samr.gov.cn/zw/zfxxgk/fdzdgknr/tssps/art/2023/art_491d5c9de75e425c8cd0203027af1d93.html" rel="nofollow">Allowed Health Food Function Claim Catalogue — Non-Nutrient Supplements (2023 Edition)</a>, with supporting technical guidance. The non-nutrient function list is closed at 24 names:

For nutrient supplements, the separate 2023 catalogue permits supplement claims for 24 nutrients and n-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids, and requires the explanatory wording to follow Annex D of GB 28050 with **no deletion, addition or merging** of the standard claim wording.

The catalogue is also being extended in the background. Under SAMR document Shi Jian Te Shi Fa [2025] No. 82, a pilot on filing of domestically produced compound-formula health food has brought 36 traditional Chinese medicinal materials — including dendrobium, gastrodia, polygonatum and astragalus — into a pilot scope. That pilot concerns domestic compound-formula products; it does not open a shortcut for imported single-ingredient SKUs today, but it signals the direction of travel.

Claims are then policed on the marketing side. Art. 78 of the Food Safety Law requires the label and instructions of a health food to avoid any disease-prevention or treatment function, to be consistent with the registered or filed content, to state the suitable and unsuitable populations and the functional component and its amount, and to carry the declaration **"this product cannot replace medicine"**. Under the <a href="https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2020/content_5488918.htm" rel="nofollow">Measures for the Administration of Advertising Review of Drugs, Medical Devices, Health Foods and Foods for Special Medical Purposes</a> (SAMR Order No. 21, in force 1 March 2020), Art. 2 prohibits publishing a health food advertisement **without prior review**, and Art. 7 requires the advertisement to follow the registration certificate or filing record and product instructions, to avoid disease prevention and treatment functions, and to state prominently that a health food is not a drug and cannot replace drug treatment.

## The cross-border route: exempt from first-import approval, not from everything else

For most supplement brands this is the route that actually gets revenue started, and it is often misunderstood as a deregulated channel. It is not deregulated — it is *differently* regulated.

Section 3 of the Circular on Improving Supervision of Cross-Border E-Commerce Retail Imports (<a href="https://www.mofcom.gov.cn/zfxxgk/gkml/art/2022/art_c44f2c0b53884baa8d07ecc5a2796325.html" rel="nofollow">Shang Cai Fa [2018] No. 486</a>, six departments including MOFCOM and GACC) provides that goods imported through the cross-border retail import channel are supervised as **articles for personal use** and are **not subject to the first-import licence, registration or filing requirements** applicable to goods — with two exceptions: goods from epidemic areas whose import has been suspended, and goods under a major quality-safety risk response. GACC's own published answers and the customs service guides restate this for food specifically: cross-border imported food is supervised as an article for personal use, no first-import licence, registration or filing is required, and the goods may arrive without Chinese labelling because they are assessed against the origin market's standards.

Three conditions still apply, and they are hard conditions:

1. **The commodity must be on the positive list.** The Cross-Border E-Commerce Retail Import Commodity List is maintained by the finance, customs and commerce authorities; GACC's January 2026 policy briefing states that the most recent amending notice is 2022 No. 7, covering 1,476 tariff lines, and that the list is adjusted dynamically. If your HS code is not on it, there is no cross-border route.
2. **Per-order and annual caps.** The 12360 hotline answers published in August 2026 confirm the limits in force: RMB 5,000 per transaction and RMB 26,000 per person per year. Figures circulating in the trade press for higher caps are not supported by an official document we can cite, and we do not repeat them.
3. **Responsibilities do not disappear.** Under the same circular, the cross-border e-commerce enterprise bears primary responsibility for quality safety and consumer protection, must entrust an enterprise registered in China and bear joint and several civil liability, and the platform must operate a risk-control mechanism and honour advance compensation. Consumers themselves need no qualification — a point GACC's January 2026 briefing makes explicitly for health products, cosmetics and infant formula.

What cross-border does **not** give you is a claim. Nothing in the circular authorises a health-function claim for a product that is not a registered or filed health food, and nothing exempts the listing copy from China's advertising law. It also does not open offline distribution: goods bought through the channel are for personal use and may not be resold into the domestic market.

<div class="statcard"><span class="n">60 + 20 / 30 / 60</span><span class="l">Working-day clocks stacked inside a registration: technical review 60 (+20), on-site verification 30, re-testing 60 — all excluded from the 20-working-day SAMR decision period</span><span class="src">Source: Health Food Registration and Filing Measures (SAMR Order No. 31), Arts. 16, 19, 20, 21, 26, 27</span></div>

## One requirement that sits outside the blue hat entirely: GACC manufacturer registration

Health food is food. For general trade import, the overseas manufacturing establishment is therefore within the scope of **GACC Decree 248**, the registration regime for overseas food manufacturers that has applied since 1 January 2022, administered by the <a href="http://www.customs.gov.cn" rel="nofollow">General Administration of Customs</a>. A blue-hat certificate and a registered factory are independent requirements: holding one does not substitute for the other.

Where the two overlap with the cross-border channel, we flag rather than assert: Shang Cai Fa [2018] No. 486 exempts the *goods* from first-import registration and filing, while Decree 248 registers the *establishment*. We have not identified an official document settling how the two interact for every HS code and bonded model, so confirm this per SKU with your customs broker before you commit stock.

## A working sequence for a supplement brand starting from zero

The order below is the one that avoids the two expensive failure modes — waiting two years with no revenue, and launching claims that have to be pulled.

1. **Strip the claims and classify.** Take every SKU and list its ingredients, dosages and the claim you want. If the claim survives the strip test, you do not need the blue hat yet; if the claim is the product, you do.
2. **Check the raw material directory first.** Directory ingredient at directory dosage with the matching directory function points at filing. Anything else points at registration.
3. **Check the origin-market gate.** For a first-import registration you need one year of marketing in the country of origin, or a documented safety report. If the SKU is too new, launch it as ordinary food or cross-border and come back later.
4. **Register the trademark before you talk to anyone.** China is a first-to-file system and distributor conversations are where marks get taken.
5. **Launch cross-border** on a positive-list HS code, with claim-free copy, to build real demand data.
6. **Run the filing or registration track in parallel**, funded by that revenue, with a Chinese agency appointed before the dossier is lodged.
7. **Fix artwork once, at the end.** Label, insert and listing copy must match the registered or filed text exactly — Art. 39 of the Implementation Regulation makes a mismatch unsellable.
8. **Add general trade** only when the certificate is in hand and the factory is GACC-registered. That is when offline pharmacy and supermarket become available.

<div class="statcard"><span class="n">6,000 m² / 8,000 m²</span><span class="l">Bonded warehousing and temperature-and-humidity-controlled warehousing operated across five Chinese cities, backed by in-house AEO advanced certification, 15 partner AEOs, 300+ enterprise clients and a peak of 540,000 orders in a single Double 11 day — the physical capacity behind a cross-border supplement launch</span><span class="src">Source: GOODSINFINITE operations data</span></div>

## What we deliberately do not assert

We would rather leave a gap than invent a number. Specifically:

- **No timeline estimate for a registration in total months.** The statutory working-day clocks are published; dossier preparation, translation and China-recognised laboratory testing are not, and any figure we gave would be our guess rather than a regulator's.
- **No fee schedule.** Neither registration nor filing has a published official fee schedule we can cite, and third-party quotes vary widely.
- **No GACC/486 interaction ruling** for cross-border consignments, as set out above.
- **No claim that cross-border authorises a health claim.** It does not, and there is no official text saying otherwise.
- **No enforcement case studies.** Penalty figures for claim violations depend on the specific provision applied and the advertising spend involved; we have not found an official text we can cite for a specific supplement case and so we quote none.
- **No statement that the 24-function catalogue is frozen.** It is maintained under the <a href="https://cfe-samr.org.cn/zcfg/bjsp_134/bmgz/202207/t20220729_4386.html" rel="nofollow">Measures for the Administration of Health Food Raw Material and Function Claim Catalogues</a> (SAMR Order No. 13, in force 1 October 2019), which provides for re-evaluation and adjustment, and a draft rule on probiotic health food was put out for public comment in July 2026 but has not been promulgated.

## FAQ

**Is a "supplement" a legal product category in China?** No. Chinese food law has no such category. Each product is either health food (requiring registration or filing and carrying the blue hat), ordinary food (sellable but silent on function), or a cross-border retail import supervised as an article for personal use. Ingredients, dosage and intended claim decide which.

**Can I sell a supplement in China as ordinary food without the blue hat?** You can sell it, but you may claim nothing. Art. 38 of the Implementation Regulation prohibits health-function claims on foods that are not health food, and Art. 39 requires the label to match the registered or filed text and forbids mixing special foods with ordinary food or drugs on the shelf.

**What is the difference between health food registration and filing?** Filing applies to directory ingredients at directory dosage with the matching directory function, and is completed on the spot where the dossier is complete. Registration applies to non-directory ingredients and to first-import health foods that are not vitamin/mineral supplements, and runs a substantive technical review of 60 working days extendable by 20, with verification and re-testing time excluded.

**How many health claims are allowed?** Twenty-four non-nutrient functions under the 2023 catalogue, plus the nutrient-supplement catalogue's 24 nutrients and n-3. Any claim outside those lists is prohibited on a food product, and the nutrient wording must follow GB 28050 Annex D without editing.

**Can I sell into China through cross-border e-commerce without a blue hat?** Generally yes. Section 3 of Shang Cai Fa [2018] No. 486 exempts cross-border retail imports from first-import licence, registration and filing, subject to the positive list (1,476 tariff lines under the 2022 No. 7 notice) and the RMB 5,000 / RMB 26,000 caps. The channel grants no claim and no offline distribution.

**Who can apply for registration?** The overseas manufacturer only, acting through a resident representative office in China or a commissioned Chinese agency, and for a first import it must produce proof of at least one year of marketing in the origin market or an overseas safety report, plus overseas package, label and instruction samples.

**Does the cross-border exemption remove GACC manufacturer registration too?** We do not assert either answer. The circular exempts the goods from first-import approval; Decree 248 registers the establishment. Confirm per HS code and channel with your broker.

## China Cross-Border E-Commerce Customer Service SLAs
Source: https://www.goods-infinite.com/insights/china-cross-border-ecommerce-customer-service
Published: 2026-10-26 · Cluster: E-commerce Operations

## China cross-border e-commerce customer service is a compliance desk, not a satisfaction desk

**China cross-border e-commerce customer service is the function that answers Chinese shoppers on marketplace channels, resolves after-sales disputes and produces the records that a platform or a regulator can later inspect, used to keep a storefront trading without penalties.** English-language org charts file it under support. In China the desk is judged on deadlines it does not set, so stop measuring it as a satisfaction centre.

The scale of after-sales exposure is documented. In 2024 market-regulation authorities across China received 18.625 million consumer complaints, and after-sales service was the largest category at 4.403 million, or 23.6 percent — top for the second consecutive year, ahead of quality at 19.5 percent ([SAMR, 2024 consumer complaint data](https://www.samr.gov.cn/xw/zj/art/2025/art_e908d62c2ce94c6cb3ec043b85158d74.html)). Complaints about "smart customer service" reached 6,969 cases, up 56.3 percent year on year, for answers that missed the question and no route to a human.

<div class="statcard"><span class="n">23.6%</span><span class="l">Share of China's 18.625 million consumer complaints in 2024 that concerned after-sales service — 4.403 million cases and the largest category for the second year running</span><span class="src">Source: SAMR, 2024 consumer complaint and report data (published 14 March 2025)</span></div>

## Five clocks run against every conversation

**A service clock is a deadline set by a statute, a regulation or a platform rule that starts when a consumer acts, used to determine how quickly a desk must respond before the cost changes.**

<div class="table-wrap"><table><thead><tr><th>Clock</th><th>What it requires</th><th>What it forces into the design</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>No-reason return</td><td>Seven days from receipt (Consumer Rights Protection Law, Art. 25; Implementing Regulation, Art. 19)</td><td>Agents approve a return without a manager, or the window closes in a queue</td></tr>
<tr><td>Regulator complaint</td><td>Accept or decline within seven working days; mediation terminated at 45 working days, 60-day outer limit (SAMR Order No. 20, Art. 14 and 21; Regulation Art. 46)</td><td>A named mainland responsible person with a mailbox that is actually read</td></tr>
<tr><td>Personal-data request</td><td>Handled and answered within fifteen working days (Network Data Security Regulation, Art. 23)</td><td>Keyword triggers in scripts and a logged escalation route</td></tr>
<tr><td>Records</td><td>Transaction, logistics, return and after-sales information kept three years from completion (SAMR Order No. 37, Art. 31)</td><td>Chat logs retrievable by order number, not buried in a vendor's archive</td></tr>
<tr><td>Platform response</td><td>Average response under 90 seconds, scored 08:00 to 23:00 only (Douyin Feige service rules)</td><td>Fifteen-hour coverage, two shifts, weekend rotation</td></tr></tbody></table></div>

## The seven-day return right cannot be opted out by default

**A no-reason return window is a statutory right of a consumer buying at a distance to cancel within seven days of receipt without giving cause, used to set the first decision an after-sales agent must be empowered to make.** Article 25 of the Consumer Rights Protection Law creates it for goods sold by network, television, telephone or mail order, excluding fresh and perishable goods, made-to-order items, digital downloads and periodicals ([Consumer Rights Protection Law, 2013 amendment](https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/2013-10/25/content_2602290.htm)).

The 2024 implementing regulation closed that room. Article 19 forbids expanding the excluded categories unilaterally, requires prominent marking and the consumer's confirmation at the point of purchase, prohibits treating exclusion as a default, and confirms that opening packaging to inspect goods does not defeat the right ([State Council Order No. 778, in force 1 July 2024](https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/content/202403/content_6940158.htm)). Refunds are made at the price actually paid, in full.

On cross-border bonded orders the legal right is not the binding constraint; the customs return procedure is. The application must be filed within 30 days, the goods must arrive within 45 days, and they must be fit for resale. A returned unit re-enters bonded stock or becomes a destruction case, so the policy has to be scripted around the customs calendar.

## A 12315 filing starts a clock that outlasts the chat

**A 12315 complaint is a consumer dispute filed on China's national market-regulation platform, used by a bureau with jurisdiction to compel a documented answer from the seller.** Jurisdiction follows the registered address: a complaint against a platform operator goes to the district bureau where the platform is registered; against a merchant, to its actual place of business or the platform operator's address ([SAMR Order No. 20, Art. 12 and 14](https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2020/content_5483878.htm)).

The bureau must decide within seven working days whether to accept the case. Mediation then runs to a hard stop: it is terminated if no agreement is reached within 45 working days of acceptance, and the 2024 regulation sets a 60-day outer limit for completing mediation. In 2024 authorities handled 24.094 million complaints and reports, up 7.2 percent, and recovered RMB 5.16 billion.

Operationally, somebody in China must answer a phone on a Chinese working day, pull the order, chat log and return record, and decide whether to settle. A brand whose only escalation path is an email alias in Europe loses on timing, and the loss is published: 13.264 million complaint entries across 5.34 million companies are already public.

## Platform scoring books silence as ten minutes

**A first-response score is the platform's measure of how long a shopper waits for a human reply, used to rank a storefront and to decide how much traffic it receives.** Douyin's service rules set the average response time standard at under 90 seconds, count only human sessions whose first message arrives between 08:00 and 22:59, and — the decisive clause — record a turn as ten minutes whenever the consumer sends a message and the merchant does not reply ([Douyin E-commerce, Feige service rules](https://school.jinritemai.com/doudian/web/articlev0/aJcDVCoeWTUH)).

<div class="statcard"><span class="n">90 seconds</span><span class="l">Ceiling on a storefront's average human response time on Douyin, scored only between 08:00 and 22:59 — and an unanswered message is booked as ten minutes</span><span class="src">Source: Douyin E-commerce, Feige service use and management rules (current revision)</span></div>

The arithmetic forces the roster. A desk that answers in fifteen seconds all day but leaves the queue unattended from 23:00 to 09:00 does not score fifteen seconds; it scores whatever the backlog drags the mean towards. Fifteen hours of coverage in two shifts with a weekend rotation is the minimum that keeps the average inside the ceiling. An out-of-hours Chinese acknowledgement does not excuse the turn, but it reduces abandoned conversations.

## Data-rights requests carry a fifteen-working-day deadline

**A personal-information request is a consumer demand to see, copy, correct, restrict or delete the data a merchant holds about them, used as the trigger for a statutory response deadline that most service scripts never mention.** Under Article 23 of the Network Data Security Regulation, a data handler must provide a convenient route for structured queries, must not restrict reasonable requests by time or location, and must handle and answer requests to copy, correct, delete, withdraw consent or close an account **within fifteen working days** ([State Council Order No. 790, in force 1 January 2025](https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202409/content_6977767.htm)).

<div class="statcard"><span class="n">15 working days</span><span class="l">Statutory window to complete and answer a consumer's request to copy, correct or delete personal data, or to close an account</span><span class="src">Source: State Council Order No. 790, Network Data Security Regulation, Art. 23 (in force 1 January 2025)</span></div>

Such a request arrives in chat dressed as something else: a shopper asking why the store still has her phone number, or asking to cancel an account. It must be recognised, logged and routed, not answered with an improvised promise. Alongside it sits a three-year retention duty on transaction, logistics, return and after-sales records, held from completion ([SAMR Order No. 37, Art. 31](https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/2021-03/15/content_5723683.htm)). The two are not contradictory — keep the commercial record, correct the personal detail on request — but assign them to different owners, or an agent will resolve the conflict by guessing.

## Three staffing models, and the stage each one fits

**A China service model is the arrangement by which a foreign brand puts Mandarin-speaking agents on a Chinese marketplace channel, used to trade without first building a mainland payroll.** Four routes exist, and they differ less on cost than on who holds the accountability.

In-house through a mainland entity gives control of scripts and escalation but needs a registered company, a payroll and hiring time before the first order. A platform partner runs the desk inside store operations: fastest to go live, hardest to keep queue discipline visible. A BPO sells dedicated seats, quoted by Chinese providers at mid four figures of renminbi per seat-month for a 7x8 position in 2026, and absorbs overnight and campaign peaks. The fourth route runs no Chinese entity at all: a Hong Kong importer of record contracts a licensed service partner that answers as provider of record, which is how a European skincare brand reached first sale in nine weeks.

Whichever route is chosen, the accountable party for a regulator complaint and a data request stays the merchant of record — name that person in writing before the first campaign.

## Script rules that keep agents out of advertising trouble

**A service script is the approved set of phrases an agent may use in a customer conversation, used to keep answers consistent and legally defensible.** In China the script is also an advertising document: Article 9 of the Advertising Law bans superlatives such as "national-level" and "best"; Article 11 requires a cited figure to carry its source and validity period; Article 28 treats a material omission as false advertising ([Advertising Law, as amended](https://policy.mofcom.gov.cn/claw/clawContent.shtml?id=90361)).

Four rules cover most of the risk. Agents may not describe a cosmetic or food product as treating or preventing disease. They may not promise a refund timetable the customs window cannot meet, because the promise is enforceable once made. They may not collect ID numbers or health details in chat. And they may not coach a consumer on how to declare an order — the declaration is the consumer's.

## The metrics that show whether a desk is compliant

**A service metric is a number reviewed on a fixed cycle to decide staffing and scripting changes, used to keep platform scores and regulator exposure inside their limits.** Speed is the easy half.

- First responses inside 90 seconds, by hour of day, so the overnight gap is visible rather than averaged away.
- Return requests approved on first contact — a proxy for whether agents hold the authority the law assumes.
- Days from approval to refund, measured against the 30/45-day customs window.
- 12315 cases per 10,000 orders, and median days to close, which is the only honest measure of regulatory exposure.
- Data-request cycle time against the fifteen-working-day limit, reported even when volume is zero.
- Repeat contact within seven days on the same order, the source of those smart-customer-service complaints.

GOODSINFINITE TRADE LIMITED acts as importer of record and bonded fulfilment partner across five locations — Tianjin, Shanghai, Ningbo, Guangzhou and Qingdao — and sits in the position where the service desk meets the customs file: our group's mainland operations file more than 20,000 customs declarations a year and peaked at 540,000 bonded orders in a single day at Double 11. After-sales matters here because a return is a customs event as well as a customer event, and the 30- and 45-day windows are ours to file. Brands keep title to their stock and their brand voice; we run the Mandarin desk, the return filings and the escalation path to a named responsible person in China. ## FAQ

**Do we need Mandarin-speaking customer service before we launch in China?** Yes, from the first order. Platform scoring is measured on human replies inside a fixed daily window, so a storefront that cannot answer in Chinese loses traffic allocation before it has revenue to protect. Three statutory clocks also start on the consumer's action rather than yours: a no-reason return request, a 12315 complaint and a request to delete personal data. The minimum viable desk is two Mandarin agents covering 09:00 to 23:00 China time with a written escalation path for regulator and data cases.

**Does the seven-day no-reason return right apply to cross-border bonded orders?** The right is written into national consumer law for distance selling, and the 2024 implementing regulation forbids expanding the excluded categories or treating exclusion as a default. The binding constraint on bonded orders is the customs return procedure: application within 30 days, arrival within 45 days, goods fit for resale. A returned unit re-enters bonded stock or becomes a destruction case, so the policy should be scripted around the customs calendar and stated on the product page.

**Can a foreign brand outsource China customer service instead of hiring?** Yes, and most do in the first year. A Tmall Global partner can run the desk inside store operations, and Chinese BPO providers sell dedicated seats, commonly quoted in the mid four figures of renminbi per seat-month for a 7x8 position in 2026. Accountability cannot be outsourced: the merchant of record remains the party named in a regulator complaint and obliged to answer a data request, so keep a named internal owner for escalations.

**What service hours should a China storefront cover?** At least 08:00 to 23:00 China time, seven days a week — the window Douyin's rules use for scoring average response time. Only human sessions starting inside that window count, and an unanswered message is booked as ten minutes, which makes overnight silence disproportionately expensive. A two-shift roster with a weekend rotation is the practical minimum, plus an out-of-hours acknowledgement in Chinese.

**What happens if a consumer complains to 12315 about our store?** The case goes to the bureau with jurisdiction over the seller's actual place of business or the platform operator's registered address, which must decide within seven working days whether to accept it. Mediation is terminated if no agreement is reached within 45 working days of acceptance, with a 60-day outer limit under the 2024 regulation. You receive a call or a platform notice and have days, not weeks, to produce the order record, chat log and return history.

## Importing Chemicals Into China: MEE Registration, Hazardous Chemical Rules and What 'China REACH' Actually Requires
Source: https://www.goods-infinite.com/insights/importing-chemicals-to-china-mee-reach
Published: 2026-10-26 · Cluster: Compliance & Registration

## Definition: what "China REACH" actually means

**"China REACH" is not a Chinese legal term. It is the informal name importers give to China's new chemical substance regime — the Measures for the Environmental Management Registration of New Chemical Substances (新化学物质环境管理登记办法, Ministry of Ecology and Environment Order No. 12), published 29 April 2020 and in force 1 January 2021, which replaced the 2010 rules (former MEP Order No. 7).**

Calling it REACH is useful shorthand but dangerous if taken literally, because EU REACH is one regulation with one dossier and one deadline, while China's system is **a set of parallel tracks that a single shipment can trip at the same time**. A chemical consignment arriving at a Chinese port may need:

1. **MEE new-substance registration** if the substance is not on the Inventory of Existing Chemical Substances in China (IECSC) — plus a Chinese agent if you apply from abroad.
2. **Hazardous chemical registration** if it appears in the national Hazardous Chemicals Catalogue — plus a business licence if you sell it.
3. **Customs inspection** with a Chinese-language GHS label and Chinese safety data sheet.
4. **A toxic chemical release notice (放行通知单)** if it is on the Catalogue of Toxic Chemicals Strictly Restricted for Import and Export in China.
5. **A MOFCOM import licence** if it is a listed drug precursor.

The five tracks have different applicants, different clocks, different competent authorities and different penalties. This article walks through each one with the article numbers, so you can check your own substance against the official text rather than against a consultant's slide.

<div class="statcard"><span class="n">47,000+ / 1,000+ / 200+</span><span class="l">Chemical substances recorded on China's Inventory of Existing Chemical Substances (IECSC), the number preliminarily screened as high-risk, and the number currently brought under a management list — stated by the Ministry of Ecology and Environment at its April 2026 press conference. Everything on the inventory is an "existing" substance; everything off it is "new" and must be registered before it is imported.</span><span class="src">Source: Ministry of Ecology and Environment regular press conference, 27 April 2026</span></div>

## Step 1 — Check the IECSC first, because it decides everything else

Under Art. 3 of MEE Order No. 12, **a "new chemical substance" is simply a chemical substance not listed on the IECSC.** If your substance is on the inventory, it is managed as an existing substance and no new-substance registration is required. There is an important trap: some inventory entries carry a **new-use environmental management** notation, and using such a substance for an industrial use other than the permitted one puts it back into the "new" category (Art. 3, second paragraph).

The IECSC is maintained and published by MEE. Its 2013 base edition (Announcement No. 1 of 2013) contained 45,612 substances, and it is supplemented in batches — most recently by MEE Announcement No. 40 of 2026 (4 August 2026), which added 4 qualifying substances and 482 already-registered new chemical substances.

Two exclusions matter commercially (Art. 2):

- **Finished products are out.** Medicines, pesticides, veterinary drugs, cosmetics, food, food additives, feed, feed additives and fertilisers are not covered — **but a new chemical substance used as a raw material or intermediate for those products is covered.** If you supply an intermediate to a Chinese cosmetic or food manufacturer, you are in scope even though the finished product is not.
- **Re-export through a bonded zone is out.** Substances imported and stored in a special customs supervision zone and exported in full without any processing are excluded. The moment they are processed, the exclusion is lost.

One inclusion catches people out: **articles designed to intentionally release a new chemical substance during normal use are in scope** for the substance they contain.

<div class="statcard"><span class="n">10 t · 1 t · < 1 t</span><span class="l">The three tonnage bands that decide which MEE track you are on: 10 tonnes or more per year produced or imported requires regular registration (常规登记); 1 tonne or more but under 10 tonnes requires simplified registration (简易登记); under 1 tonne — or a polymer whose monomer or reactant content does not exceed 2%, or a low-concern polymer — requires filing (备案). A substance with a regular registration certificate is added to the IECSC five years after first registration.</span><span class="src">Source: MEE Order No. 12, Arts. 10 and 44</span></div>

## Step 2 — Pick the right MEE track, and budget for the right clock

<table>
  <thead><tr><th>Track</th><th>Trigger (Art. 10)</th><th>Core dossier</th><th>Technical review</th><th>Decision</th></tr></thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr><td><strong>Regular registration 常规登记</strong></td><td>10 t/yr or more produced or imported</td><td>Application form; physico-chemical, health toxicology and ecotoxicology test reports; <strong>environmental risk assessment report</strong>; signed and sealed commitment to implement or pass down risk control measures (Art. 15). High-hazard substances additionally require a socio-economic benefit analysis</td><td>60 days or fewer (Art. 25)</td><td>Within 20 working days of acceptance, extendable by 10; review time excluded</td></tr>
    <tr><td><strong>Simplified registration 简易登记</strong></td><td>1 t/yr or more and under 10 t/yr</td><td>Application form; physico-chemical properties plus persistence, bioaccumulation and aquatic toxicity data; signed and sealed risk-control commitment (Art. 16)</td><td>30 days or fewer (Art. 25)</td><td>Same 20 + 10 working days</td></tr>
    <tr><td><strong>Filing 备案</strong></td><td>Under 1 t/yr; polymer with monomer or reactant content of 2% or less; low-concern polymer</td><td>Filing form plus evidence of the qualifying condition (Art. 36). MEE archives complete materials and issues a receipt — <strong>you may start the activity once you file</strong> (Art. 37)</td><td>None</td><td>None</td></tr>
  </tbody>
</table>

Three practical points that change planning:

1. **Ecotoxicology must use Chinese test organisms.** Art. 15 and Art. 16 both require ecotoxicology test reports to include data generated with test organisms of China under the relevant standards. Data packages built only for EU or US submission usually need top-up testing. Domestic labs must hold testing-institution qualification and, for health/eco toxicology, comply with GLP; overseas labs must meet internationally accepted GLP requirements (Art. 14).
2. **Certificate contents are narrow, and they bind you.** Art. 26 lists what the certificate states: type, applicant and agent, identifiers, **the applied use**, **the applied tonnage**, activity type and risk control measures. Exceeding the tonnage, switching from import to production, changing the use or changing the risk control measures all require a fresh application (Art. 29). A successful trial order therefore does not authorise commercial volume.
3. **Filing does not entitle you to be listed on the IECSC.** Only regular registration leads to inclusion, five years after first registration (Art. 44); simplified and filed substances are expressly not listed.

### The post-registration obligations nobody budgets for

Registration is not the end. Under Chapter IV of MEE Order No. 12:

- **Downstream information transfer** (Art. 38): certificate or filing receipt number, applied use, hazard characteristics and risk control measures, and environmental management requirements must be passed to downstream users, who may demand them.
- **Records** (Art. 39): regular and simplified registration materials and activity records must be kept at least **10 years**; filing materials and activity records at least **3 years**.
- **Public disclosure** (Art. 40): holders of regular registrations must publish implementation of risk control measures via their own website or another publicly accessible channel.
- **First activity report** (Art. 41): within **60 days** of first production, or of first import and transfer to a processor using the substance.
- **Annual report** (Art. 41): where the certificate requires it, by **30 April** each year from the year after registration.
- **New hazard reporting** (Art. 42): any newly identified environmental or health hazard or risk must be reported, and MEE may then vary or withdraw the certificate.

<div class="statcard"><span class="n">2,828 / 3 years</span><span class="l">Entries in the Hazardous Chemicals Catalogue (2015 edition) — the practical definition of a "hazardous chemical" for import purposes — and the validity period of a hazardous chemical registration certificate, which must be renewed on application three months before expiry. Registration is required before the first import, not after.</span><span class="src">Source: State Council Order No. 591; former SAWS Order No. 53, Arts. 10 and 16; Guangxi Department of Emergency Management implementation notice</span></div>

## Step 3 — If it is on the Hazardous Chemicals Catalogue, a second regulator appears

The environmental track and the safety track are independent. A substance can be an existing substance on the IECSC (no MEE registration) and still be a listed hazardous chemical (full safety regime). The governing instrument is the **Regulation on the Safety Management of Hazardous Chemicals (State Council Order No. 591, in force 1 December 2011, amended by State Council Order No. 645 of 2013)**, which defines a hazardous chemical by its properties — toxic, corrosive, explosive, flammable, oxidising — and delegates the catalogue to the competent authority.

What an importer must do:

<table>
  <thead><tr><th>Requirement</th><th>Legal basis</th><th>Timing / detail</th></tr></thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr><td><strong>Hazardous chemical registration</strong></td><td>Order No. 53, Arts. 2 and 10</td><td>An importing enterprise must register <strong>before the first import</strong>; one registration covers the same variety from the same manufacturer</td></tr>
    <tr><td><strong>Content of registration</strong></td><td>Order No. 53, Art. 12</td><td>Classification and label information, physical and chemical properties, main uses, hazard characteristics, storage/use/transport safety requirements, emergency response measures</td></tr>
    <tr><td><strong>Certificate validity</strong></td><td>Order No. 53, Art. 16</td><td>3 years; apply for renewal 3 months before expiry</td></tr>
    <tr><td><strong>Change notification</strong></td><td>Order No. 53, Art. 15</td><td>Within 15 working days if name, address, registered varieties or emergency number change, or a new hazard characteristic is found</td></tr>
    <tr><td><strong>24-hour emergency telephone</strong></td><td>Order No. 53, Art. 22</td><td>The importer must provide — itself, or through its import agent or the registration body — a domestically staffed 24-hour emergency consultation line, <strong>and print that number on the safety label</strong></td></tr>
    <tr><td><strong>Business licence if you sell</strong></td><td>Order No. 55, Art. 3</td><td>No unit or individual may trade in hazardous chemicals, including warehousing operations, without a hazardous chemical business licence</td></tr>
  </tbody>
</table>

Order No. 53's review chain is fully timed: the provincial registration office makes a preliminary review within **3 working days**, reviews materials within **20 working days**, and the national registration centre completes its review within **15 working days** (Art. 13).

**A caution on the documents.** Arts. 14 and 31 of Order No. 53 list the foreign-trade operator registration form (对外贸易经营者备案登记表) among the documents an importer must produce. That registration was abolished on 30 December 2022, when the NPC Standing Committee deleted Art. 9 of the Foreign Trade Law. The 2012 rule has not been re-issued to match, so confirm with the provincial registration office which substitute documents it accepts before you assemble the file.

**Enforcement is real and it is published.** In a case released by the Shanghai Municipal Emergency Management Bureau in January 2025, a trading company in Changning District was found on inspection to have imported six catalogue chemicals, including UV-curing adhesive and a nano dispersion, without completing registration. It was fined **RMB 20,000** on 9 July 2024 under Art. 78(1)(12) of State Council Order No. 591.

## Step 4 — Customs inspection: the Chinese label and the Chinese SDS

Even with every certificate in hand, the shipment is inspected at the border. **GACC Announcement No. 129 of 2020** (issued 18 December 2020, in force 10 January 2021, replacing former AQSIQ Announcement No. 30 of 2012) sets out what customs checks for chemicals on the current national catalogue.

At declaration, the consignee or its agent must enter the hazard class, packing group (except for bulk), UN number and UN packaging mark (except for bulk), and provide:

1. a **Declaration of Conformity for Importing Hazardous Chemical Enterprises** (prescribed form, Annex 1);
2. for products requiring inhibitors or stabilisers, a statement of the actual inhibitor or stabiliser added and the quantity;
3. **samples of the Chinese hazardous-property label and the Chinese safety data sheet**.

Customs then inspects whether the main components, physical and chemical characteristics and hazard class conform to the applicable requirements, whether the package carries a Chinese label and is accompanied by a Chinese SDS, and whether the packaging type, mark, category, specification, unit weight and condition conform (Announcement No. 129, Sections 5–6). Where the chemical is used as a food or food additive, food safety rules also apply.

The standards behind those labels are the GHS implementation standards — the **GB 30000 series** on classification and labelling of chemicals and **GB 15258** on the preparation of chemical safety labels, with SDS format standards including **GB/T 17519-2013**. Chinese-language labels and SDS are not a translation afterthought; they are a customs inspection item, which means a labelling defect stops the container, not the marketing launch.

<div class="statcard"><span class="n">60 days / 30 days / 20+10</span><span class="l">The MEE statutory clocks: technical review may not exceed 60 days for regular registration or 30 days for simplified registration, and the registration decision must be issued within 20 working days of acceptance, extendable by 10. Technical review time sits outside the decision period, so the elapsed calendar time to a certificate is driven mainly by how long your test data takes to generate — not by the regulator.</span><span class="src">Source: MEE Order No. 12, Art. 25</span></div>

## Step 5 — Two lists that can stop the shipment outright

### Toxic chemicals strictly restricted for import and export

China implements the Stockholm, Minamata and Rotterdam conventions plus its own new-pollutants agenda through the **Catalogue of Toxic Chemicals Strictly Restricted for Import and Export in China**, published in October 2023 by MEE, MOFCOM and GACC, replacing the 2020 edition. The current catalogue covers nine categories including PFOS and its salts, mercury, tetra-methyl and tetra-ethyl lead, polychlorinated terphenyls, tributyltin compounds, short-chain chlorinated paraffins, decabromodiphenyl ether, and PFOA and its salts and related compounds.

**Anyone importing or exporting a listed toxic chemical must apply to MEE for a Toxic Chemical Import/Export Environmental Management Release Notice (有毒化学品进(出)口环境管理放行通知单) and present that notice to customs to clear the goods.** There is no discretionary alternative route.

Overlapping this, the **Key Controlled New Pollutants List (2023 edition)** (MEE and five other departments, Order No. 28, in force 1 March 2023) sets per-substance control measures. For PFOS, for example, the listed measures required a release notice for any import or export and then **prohibited import and export from 1 January 2024**. If your substance appears on either list, the commercial question is usually not "how do we register it" but "is it still importable at all".

### Drug precursors

The **Regulation on the Administration of Precursor Chemicals (State Council Order No. 445, in force 1 November 2005, thrice amended)** applies a classified licensing system to production, trading, purchase, transport and import/export. Import requires:

- an **import licence** from MOFCOM or a commerce department it delegates, issued after review within **20 days** (Arts. 26 and 27);
- an **international verification procedure** for substances on the verification catalogue, with verification time excluded from the licensing period (Art. 29);
- presentation of the licence to customs, which clears the goods against it (Art. 30).

Two provisions catch importers by surprise. First, **moving precursors from abroad into a bonded zone, export processing zone or other special customs supervision area is treated as import** and needs the licence; movements *within* China into or between those zones do not (Art. 30, paragraphs 2 and 3). Second, **Art. 5 makes the regime cumulative**: where a precursor is also a drug or a hazardous chemical, the drug and hazardous chemical rules apply on top. Import and export of precursors outside the licensing system carries criminal liability.

## What the penalties actually look like

The fines are not the real risk for most importers. The **1-year and 3-year application bans** are, because they freeze your entire China pipeline across every substance in your portfolio, not just the one that failed.

## The eight-step sequence we run before a chemical shipment

1. **Fix the substance identity** — CAS number, composition, and whether the product is a substance, a mixture or an article that intentionally releases.
2. **Screen the IECSC** — on the inventory (existing) or off it (new)? If on it, check for a new-use management notation on your intended use.
3. **Screen the Hazardous Chemicals Catalogue (2015 edition)** — if listed, plan hazardous chemical registration before first import, and a business licence if you will sell domestically.
4. **Screen the restricted toxic chemicals catalogue and the new pollutants list** — if listed, apply for the MEE release notice, or confirm whether the substance is already prohibited.
5. **Screen the precursor schedules** — if listed, build the MOFCOM import licence and international verification into the shipment timeline.
6. **Choose the MEE track by real forecast tonnage** — regular, simplified or filing — and generate the Chinese-organism ecotoxicology data early, because that is the long pole.
7. **Appoint the Chinese agent and sign the agency contract** — MEE requires the applicant and agent to jointly perform obligations; the contract must cover replacement of the agent and run for the life of the certificate.
8. **Prepare the Chinese GHS label and Chinese SDS before shipment** — plus the Declaration of Conformity, the UN number and packaging marks for the declaration, and confirm the receiving warehouse is licensed for the hazard class.

## Where a bonded model does and does not fit

Bonded warehousing is a genuine advantage for non-hazardous industrial chemicals, raw materials and formulated products: you can land stock, hold it under customs supervision, and release it into the domestic market as orders arrive, deferring duty and VAT until release. We operate **6,000㎡ of bonded warehousing and 8,000㎡ of temperature- and humidity-controlled warehousing** through our network, alongside 300+ enterprises served and our own AEO advanced certification plus 15 partner AEO facilities, with fulfilment across five Chinese cities.

It is equally important to say where it does not fit. **A listed hazardous chemical cannot sit in a conventional bonded warehouse.** Art. 24 of State Council Order No. 591 requires storage in a dedicated warehouse, dedicated site or dedicated storage room under a designated person, with additional safety facilities, and a business licence is required for warehousing operations. For those products the correct structure is a licensed dangerous-goods warehouse, a qualified domestic carrier and an emergency response arrangement — and the classification has to be settled before the vessel sails.

## What we deliberately do not assert

This article stays with what the official text says. Four things commonly claimed in vendor and law-firm content we will not repeat:

1. **There is no official fee schedule or fixed calendar duration for MEE registration, so we give none.** The statute fixes technical review and decision periods, not total elapsed time; the variable is testing.
2. **We do not claim an equivalence or mutual recognition between EU REACH and MEE Order No. 12.** Art. 14 permits overseas test institutions that meet internationally accepted GLP requirements to generate health and eco toxicology data, which reduces duplication, but it is not recognition of a foreign registration.
3. **We do not state a customs clearance time for chemical imports.** Clearance depends on declaration mode, inspection selection and enterprise credit grade; no single statutory figure exists.
4. **We do not advise whether a specific substance is or is not on a catalogue.** That is a substance-by-substance determination against the current published lists and MEE's technical identification service, not a general conclusion.
