## Bilibili Marketing for Foreign Brands in China
Source: https://www.goods-infinite.com/insights/bilibili-marketing-foreign-brands-china
Published: 2026-10-05 · Cluster: Marketing & New Media

Most Western brands file Bilibili under "curiosity": a Chinese video site full of animation clips and gaming commentary. That classification is expensive. Bilibili is where a large share of China's urban under-35 consumers — the cohort that adopts premium imported goods years before the mainstream — spends close to two hours a day, and advertising revenue there grew 28% year over year in the second quarter of 2026 because brand budgets followed them in. This guide covers who is actually on the platform, how its two commercial routes work, what Chinese advertising law demands of a creator campaign, and how the content connects to a compliant cross-border checkout.

<div class="statcard"><span class="n">116.5 million</span><span class="l">Bilibili average daily active users in Q2 2026, each spending 113 minutes a day on the app — total user time up 14% year over year</span><span class="src">Source: Bilibili Inc. Q2 2026 unaudited results, quarter ended 30 June 2026</span></div>

## Bilibili is a Chinese interest-circle video community, used by brands to reach urban consumers under 35

Bilibili (B站) is a video community organised around interest circles — animation, games, technology, automobiles, home, knowledge — used by brands as a consideration channel rather than a sales channel. Its structure matters more than its size. QuestMobile data cited in the company's 2026 disclosures puts Bilibili's penetration at roughly **70% of China's Z+ generation** (people born between 1985 and 2009), with an average active-user age of **26.5** and new users averaging **22.5**. About half the audience is female, **51%** sit in tier-1 and new tier-1 cities, and **40% of daily active users** watch video or live-commerce content on the platform.

That profile is why the platform converts in high-ticket categories that need explanation: premium skincare, medical-adjacent devices, smart home hardware, outdoor gear and consumer electronics.

<div class="statcard"><span class="n">70%</span><span class="l">Share of China's Z+ generation (born 1985–2009) who use Bilibili, with an average active-user age of 26.5</span><span class="src">Source: QuestMobile, as cited in Bilibili Q1 2026 company disclosure (February 2026 measurement)</span></div>

## Mid-form video is content longer than five minutes, used by brands to explain products a 15-second clip cannot

Bilibili's core inventory is mid-form video, typically five to twenty minutes. The commercial case is not aesthetic. Bilibili and the measurement firm Miaozhen ran eye-tracking and EEG tests with more than a hundred participants and found that viewers recalled a brand name **nearly 26% more often** after mid-form video than after short video, with recall of complex product information measured at **74.0%**. Bilibili users' comment rate was **2.8 times** the video-media average in the same study.

The platform's own 2026 second-quarter numbers point the same way: watch time on videos longer than five minutes grew **18% year over year**, and video podcasts alone passed 100 million viewing minutes a day. For a foreign brand, this is the one Chinese channel where a technically literate creator can spend ten minutes dismantling a product's engineering and be rewarded for it.

## Huahuo is Bilibili's official creator-collaboration marketplace, used to brief, price and pay UP主

Huahuo (花火, at huahuo.bilibili.com) is the platform's official creator-brand marketplace, built so that paid collaborations run through a system handling creator matching, quoting, contracting, order management and post-campaign data rather than a direct message and a bank transfer. Creators on Bilibili are called **UP主**; a collaboration bought through Huahuo is called a **商单**.

### Boost is Bilibili's content-amplification product, used to extend a video that already works

The second route is **Boost** (起飞), Bilibili's content-amplification product. Once a video is published, Boost buys it additional distribution at CPM or CPC rates. The two are designed to work as a pair: seed with Huahuo collaborations across relevant interest circles, then concentrate paid amplification on the videos that earned organic traction. Bilibili and Miaozhen report audience overlap between the original reach and the amplified reach of around **10%**, and that more than **20%** of videos under this combined approach halve their cost per video view.

The operational snag for an overseas brand is account access. Advertiser onboarding on Bilibili expects a Chinese business licence whose registered scope matches the promoted content, industry qualification documents, a corporate payment account, and — for a standalone landing page — an ICP filing. An entity incorporated in Europe or North America cannot complete that file alone. In practice foreign brands either appoint a licensed domestic agency that contracts as the advertiser of record, or work with an in-market partner that already operates stores and ad accounts in China. Whoever holds the account also holds the legal exposure.

## The Internet Advertising Measures are China's online advertising rules, used to decide when a creator video is legally an advertisement

The Internet Advertising Measures (SAMR Order No. 72, published 25 February 2023, in force since **1 May 2023**) are the operative rules, and they are more specific than most foreign marketing teams expect. Article 2 applies them to any commercial promotion delivered through a Chinese internet medium, regardless of where the advertiser is domiciled — so a campaign targeting mainland users is captured even if the contract is signed in London or Los Angeles.

### Four provisions that change how you brief a creator

- **Article 9** requires internet advertising to be identifiable, and states that promotion through knowledge explanation, experience sharing or consumption review *with a purchase link attached* must be conspicuously marked "广告". A Bilibili review video with a Tmall Global link is therefore an advertisement, and must say so.
- **Article 13** places responsibility for truthfulness on the advertiser and requires self-published advertising records to be kept for **at least three years**; **Article 14** obliges the agency and the platform to verify the advertiser's real identity and keep the same three-year file.
- **Article 15** extends that file to algorithmically delivered advertising, which must log the recommendation rules and the delivery records. On an algorithmic feed, that makes the media plan a compliance document.
- **Article 19** provides that a seller promoting goods through live streaming bears advertiser duties, and that a host recommending a product in their own name bears **advertising endorser** duties.
- **Article 25** routes a failure of identifiability to Article 59(3) of the Advertising Law: correction, plus a fine on the ad publisher of **up to RMB 100,000**.

Two further rules catch foreign brands specifically. Advertising Law Article 38 bars endorsers from recommending goods they have not used, with Article 61 permitting confiscation of gains plus a fine of one to two times those gains — so a UP主 who never touched your product is a liability. And Article 11 requires any figure, statistic or survey used in an advertisement to be truthful and sourced, with its scope and validity period stated. "Clinically proven" without the study, its date and its limits is a defect, not a flourish.

<div class="table-wrap"><table><tr><th>Campaign element</th><th>What Chinese rules require</th><th>Who is accountable</th></tr><tr><td>Creator video with a shopping link</td><td>Conspicuous "广告" label (Measures, Art. 9)</td><td>Ad publisher; advertiser for truthfulness</td></tr><tr><td>Live-stream selling</td><td>Advertiser duties on the seller; endorser duties on the host (Art. 19)</td><td>Brand and host separately</td></tr><tr><td>Data, statistics, survey claims</td><td>Truthful, sourced, scope and validity stated (Advertising Law, Art. 11)</td><td>Advertiser</td></tr><tr><td>Creator endorsement</td><td>Creator must have used the product (Advertising Law, Art. 38)</td><td>Endorser, plus the brand</td></tr><tr><td>Ad and delivery records</td><td>Kept at least three years, including algorithm and delivery logs (Art. 13–15)</td><td>Agency and advertiser</td></tr><tr><td>Impacted categories</td><td>Pre-publication ad review for medical devices, health food and similar (Art. 7)</td><td>Advertiser, before publishing</td></tr></table></div>

## Content asset measurement is the practice of valuing a video after its posting window, used to decide where the next yuan goes

Content asset measurement on Bilibili means tracking a video's commercial value beyond its launch week, because the platform's recommenders keep serving good mid-form content long after publication. The signals are comment density and long-comment share, brand-name search lift inside Bilibili, cost per video view after Boost, and tracked store clicks. Set all four up before the first brief; Chinese agencies otherwise report reach by default.

### What concentrated spend looks like in practice

The benchmark worth internalising is concentration. Bilibili's own 2025 marketing casebook, reported by Chinese business media, describes a beauty brand that paired a hero product with outdoor creators and an in-app themed campaign and ended up with **60% of its quarterly new customers** on the platform, and another that reported an average return above **10:1** with a new-customer rate over 70%. A consumer electronics brand pushed a **RMB 50,000** flagship through a hardcore technology creator and reported triple-digit return on a single video. The pattern in every case is fewer, longer, more technical videos, amplified hard after they prove themselves.

<div class="statcard"><span class="n">RMB 100,000</span><span class="l">Maximum fine on the ad publisher for advertising that is not identifiable — the exposure created by an unlabelled creator video with a shopping link</span><span class="src">Source: Advertising Law of the PRC, Art. 59(3), as applied via Internet Advertising Measures Art. 9 and 25 (2023)</span></div>

## Cross-border retail import is the customs regime that lets a foreign brand sell to Chinese consumers without a domestic entity

Cross-border retail import is the customs regime under which consumers buy directly from an overseas seller, used by foreign brands to enter China without establishing a domestic company. Bilibili content does not sell by itself; it points to a storefront, and for most foreign brands that is a cross-border one — Tmall Global, JD Worldwide, Douyin or a brand-owned mini program — fulfilled from a bonded warehouse.

The tax arithmetic is stable. Under the Ministry of Finance, GACC and STA statement Cai Guan Shui [2018] No. 49, the single-order limit is **RMB 5,000** and the annual individual limit **RMB 26,000**; inside those limits tariffs are temporarily **0%**, and import VAT and consumption tax are levied at **70% of the statutory amount**. For a standard 13% VAT good that is an effective **9.1%**. High-end cosmetics priced above RMB 10 per millilitre or gram — or RMB 15 per piece — also attract the 15% consumption tax, which pushes the all-in figure toward **23.1%**. Above the annual limit, the consignment reverts to general trade treatment.

Two consequences follow for a marketing plan. First, the price you can advertise in a creator video is a landed price your supply chain has to reach, so the media brief and the logistics quote are the same conversation. Second, the product must appear on the cross-border retail import list — 1,476 tariff lines as last adjusted. If your SKU is not on it, no amount of creator content will make it sellable through that channel.

## FAQ

**Can a foreign brand buy media on Bilibili without a China entity?** Not directly. Bilibili's advertiser onboarding expects a Chinese business licence, industry qualification documents and a corporate payment account, and landing pages normally need an ICP filing. Overseas brands therefore work through a licensed domestic agency or an in-market partner that already holds the account and the contracting entity, and that partner becomes the party legally responsible for the ad file.

**What is Huahuo on Bilibili?** Huahuo (huahuo.bilibili.com) is Bilibili's official creator-collaboration marketplace. It handles creator matching, quoting, contracting, order management and performance data in one system, so a brand briefs and pays creators through the platform rather than through informal direct messages. It is the compliant route for a paid brand collaboration with a UP主.

**Do Bilibili creator videos have to be labelled as advertising?** Yes, when they add a purchase route. Article 9 of the Internet Advertising Measures (SAMR Order No. 72, effective 1 May 2023) requires that content which promotes goods through knowledge explanation, experience sharing or consumption review and attaches a shopping link be conspicuously marked "广告" (advertisement). Non-identifiable advertising exposes the ad publisher to a fine of up to RMB 100,000 under Article 59(3) of the Advertising Law.

**How long does a Bilibili campaign take to produce results?** Longer than on short-video platforms, and that is the point. Mid-form videos are indexed and recommended for months, so the realistic planning horizon is a quarter, not a week. Budget for a seeding phase of eight to twelve creator videos, measure comment and re-boost behaviour in the first two weeks, then concentrate spend on the videos that earned organic search lift.

**How should a foreign brand measure success on Bilibili?** Use four signals rather than view counts: comment density and long-comment share, on-platform search lift for your brand name, cost per video view after amplification, and downstream store traffic from tracked links. Platform-reported brand cases show that concentrated spend behind a proven video outperforms spreading the same budget across many creators.

## How Long Does Customs Clearance Take in China? (2026 Timelines)
Source: https://www.goods-infinite.com/insights/how-long-does-customs-clearance-take-china
Published: 2026-10-05 · Cluster: Compliance & Registration

## Definition: what "customs clearance time in China" actually measures

"Customs clearance time" in China is **not a single statutory number**. It is the elapsed time between the moment your declaration is accepted by the General Administration of Customs (GACC) and the moment goods are released — and it is shaped by three variables the law lets vary: **your declaration mode, whether your goods are selected for inspection, and your enterprise's credit status (AEO)**.

The legally fixed part is the **declaration deadline** (not the clearance speed): importers must declare within **14 days** of the transport's entry declaration, or pay a demurrage fee (滞报金). The clearance *speed* itself is a function of how compliant and well-prepared your filing is.

## The official baseline: clearance is fast for compliant goods

China has deliberately compressed clearance time through its **Smart Customs (智慧海关)** programme. At the State Council Information Office briefing on 13 January 2025, GACC stated that for **low-risk, compliant goods**, the process from declaration to release is handled fully online and is essentially **"second-level" clearance (读秒通关)** — i.e. near-instant once the system accepts the declaration.

<div class="statcard"><span class="n">秒级</span><span class="l">For low-risk, compliant goods under Smart Customs, GACC states release from declaration to release is essentially "second-level" (near-instant) when filed fully electronically</span><span class="src">Source: State Council Information Office briefing, 13 January 2025 (China.org.cn)</span></div>

This is the honest headline: **if your paperwork is clean, your goods are not inspected, and your declaration is accepted automatically, clearance is the same day — often within minutes.** The variability everyone worries about comes from the inspection and manual-review steps, not from a slow baseline.

## The three variables that move the clock

### 1. Declaration mode — two-step declaration (两步申报)

China's **two-step declaration** is the single biggest structural lever on clearance time. Formalised in **GACC Decree No. 277 (Measures for the Declaration and Management of Import and Export Goods)** and refined by the **2025 optimisation pilot** (piloted from 6 May 2025 at 9 regional customs authorities across 11 sites), it works like this:

- **Step 1 — summary declaration (概要申报):** the importer files a reduced set of fields. If the goods are not subject to tax, licence, or inspection holds, they can be **taken away from the port (提离)** immediately after summary acceptance.
- **Step 2 — complete declaration (完整申报):** the remaining fields are lodged **within 14 days** of the transport's entry declaration.

<div class="statcard"><span class="n">14 days</span><span class="l">Statutory window to lodge the complete declaration after the transport's entry declaration under two-step declaration — miss it and a demurrage fee (滞报金) applies</span><span class="src">Source: GACC Decree No. 277 (Measures for Declaration and Management of Import and Export Goods); gov.cn policy interpretation, April 2025</span></div>

A related mechanism, **advance declaration (提前申报)**, lets importers file before goods physically arrive — for imports, after departure and before arrival; for exports, within seven days before arrival at the customs supervision zone. Both move the clerical work *ahead* of the cargo so release is not blocked at the gate.

### 2. Inspection selection (查验) — the real time variable

When goods are picked for inspection, time becomes genuinely variable. Risk-based selection depends on the product category: food, cosmetics, medical devices, and electronics carry higher inspection probability than general merchandise. China is compressing this too — GACC's **remote inspection (远程查检 / "千里眼")** reform cuts single-inspection job time by about **90%** versus on-site inspection, and vacuum-packaged high-tech goods get a dedicated non-intrusive inspection mode that cuts clearance time by about **80%**.

> Practical read: you cannot eliminate inspection risk, but you can shrink its impact by getting product compliance right *before* arrival — see our [China customs clearance process guide](china-customs-clearance-process.html).

### 3. AEO status — the credit-tier shortcut

An **AEO (Authorised Economic Operator, 高级认证企业)** is the highest credit tier in China's customs system, and it is the most reliable way to keep clearance fast and predictable.

<div class="statcard"><span class="n">&lt;20%</span><span class="l">An AEO enterprise's average inspection rate is below 20% of the rate applied to ordinary enterprises, plus priority handling and a dedicated coordinator</span><span class="src">Source: GACC AEO management measures (Decree No. 251 and implementing notices)</span></div>

AEO benefits are codified in GACC's management measures and include: priority clearance, a substantially lower inspection rate, the ability to apply for bond waivers, reduced audit frequency, and — in emergencies — the ability to request clearance outside normal working hours with as little as 8 hours' notice. China currently has AEO mutual recognition with **52 countries and regions**, so the status also speeds you through partner customs abroad.

## A realistic clearance timeline, by scenario

| Scenario | Typical release | Why |
|----------|----------------|-----|
| Low-risk goods, clean e-declaration, no inspection | Same day, often minutes | Smart Customs auto-accepts; "second-level" release |
| Two-step summary declaration, non-held goods | Goods leave port before full declaration | Summary acceptance triggers 提离 |
| Goods selected for inspection | Variable; remote inspection cuts job time ~90% | Risk-based 查验 + modernised inspection |
| Manual review (wrong HS / value / missing licence) | Hours to days | Declaration bounced for correction |
| Regulated product, compliance not done upstream | Blocked until fixed | GACC/NMPA/CCC registration must clear first |

The lesson: **the clock is mostly in your control.** Inspection and manual review are the only real unknowns; everything else is preparation.

## FAQ

**How long does customs clearance take in China?** There is no single statutory duration. For low-risk, fully-compliant goods under Smart Customs, GACC states release from declaration to release is essentially "second-level" (near-instant) when filed electronically. Declarations not selected for inspection typically clear the day they are accepted; time only becomes variable when goods are inspected or the declaration needs manual review.

**What is two-step declaration and does it speed up clearance?** Two-step declaration (两步申报) lets you lodge a summary declaration first; compliant goods can be taken away from the port before the full declaration is finished. The complete declaration must be lodged within 14 days of the transport's entry declaration, or a late-declaration fee applies. It is formalised in GACC Decree No. 277 and refined by the 2025 optimisation pilot.

**Do AEO-certified companies clear customs faster?** Yes. AEO (高级认证企业) is China Customs' top credit tier: its average inspection rate is below 20% of ordinary enterprises, with priority handling, a dedicated coordinator, and mutual recognition across 52 countries and regions.

**What makes clearance slow?** Inspection selection (查验), incorrect or incomplete declarations (wrong HS code, value mismatch, missing licences), and upstream product-compliance gaps (GACC/NMPA/CCC not done before arrival). Fixing these at origin is what saves time.

**How long do I have to declare imported goods?** Within 14 days of the transport's entry declaration; under two-step declaration this window applies to the complete declaration after an initial summary. Late declaration incurs a daily demurrage fee from the 15th day.

## China Cosmetics Reforms 2025–2026: China-First Launch, Animal-Testing Waivers & Filing Relief
Source: https://www.goods-infinite.com/insights/china-cosmetics-2025-2026-reforms
Published: 2026-10-02 · Cluster: Compliance & Registration

## Definition: what the 2025–2026 cosmetics reforms actually change

The "2025–2026 China cosmetics reforms" are a two-step deregulation package from the **National Medical Products Administration (NMPA)** that lowers the cost and time of bringing both imported and domestic cosmetics to market — without lowering safety standards. Step one is a strategic **Opinion** (24 reform measures); step two is an implementing **Announcement** (eight concrete measures) that brands can act on today.

The headline wins for an overseas brand: you can now **launch a new product in China before it sells anywhere else**, you may **skip animal testing on more product types**, and the **paperwork for filing and registration got lighter**. Below is the precise, sourced detail — and where the old rules still apply.

## The two documents, in order

China's cosmetics regime sits under the **Cosmetics Supervision and Administration Regulation (CSAR, 化妆品监督管理条例)**, in force since 1 January 2021, and its implementing **Administrative Measures for Cosmetics Registration and Filing** (化妆品注册备案管理办法). Every reform below works *within* that framework.

<div class="statcard"><span class="n">¥1.1 trillion</span><span class="l">China's cosmetics retail market size in 2025 — now the largest cosmetics consumer market in the world, which is why NMPA is racing to make market entry faster</span><span class="src">Source: China Pharmaceutical News (中国医药报, NMPA's official newspaper), 4 August 2026</span></div>

<div class="statcard"><span class="n">8 measures</span><span class="l">in NMPA Announcement 2026 No. 70, effective 29 July 2026, cutting filing and registration burden for imported and domestic cosmetics</span><span class="src">Source: NMPA Announcement 2026 No. 70</span></div>

**1. The Opinion — 国药监妆〔2025〕18号.** Published 17 November 2025, this 24-measure policy paper ([full text on gov.cn](https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202511/content_7048797.htm)) set the direction: encourage international new products to launch in China first, accelerate animal-testing waivers (measure 23), and simplify registration/filing data. It is the "why"; the Announcement is the "how."

**2. The Announcement — 2026 No. 70.** Issued 28 July 2026 and effective 29 July 2026 ([full text on nmpa.gov.cn](https://www.nmpa.gov.cn/xxgk/fgwj/gzwj/gzwjhzhp/20260729115807198.html)), it turns the Opinion into eight operational measures. This is the document your regulatory affairs team will actually apply.

## Measure 1 — "China-first launch" (中国首发): no more overseas-sales proof

Before this reform, an imported cosmetic had to show it was **already marketed in its country of origin or production** before China would register or file it. Obtaining that proof typically took **one to two months**, which is why many global launches reached Chinese consumers later than everyone else.

Under Announcement 2026 No. 70, an international new product that **launches first in China** — or **simultaneously with other markets** — can instead submit a **commitment declaration of China-first launch** and skip the overseas-sales proof entirely. Even the production-country sales packaging can be submitted as a **design drawing**. Industry commentary (quoted in China Pharmaceutical News) estimates this can bring a global launch to China roughly **six months earlier**.

> Practical read: if your global launch calendar puts China on the list, you no longer have to ship and sell a batch abroad first just to satisfy Chinese paperwork.

## Measure 2 — expanded animal-testing waivers

China never instituted a blanket animal-testing ban, but the exemption has been widening:

- **Since 1 May 2021:** imported **general cosmetics** can be exempt from mandatory animal testing if conditions are met — a home-country GMP/quality-management certificate, a complete safety assessment, and the product is not intended for infants or children.
- **From 29 July 2026:** the waiver extends to **certain special cosmetics** — **perming products, non-oxidative hair dye, and spot-whitening products with only physical covering action** — and to **ordinary cosmetics that use new raw materials (excluding children's cosmetics)**, provided the manufacturer holds a home-country quality-system certificate **and** the safety risk assessment fully confirms safety. NMPA can widen the scope later via technical guidelines.

What this does **not** change: most special-use cosmetics (sunscreen, whitening with active agents, hair dye beyond the listed types, anti-hair-loss) and **children's cosmetics** still require toxicology data. Confirm per SKU.

## Measures 3–8 — the "filing relief" package

The rest of Announcement 2026 No. 70 is about cutting redundant work:

- **Raw-material data simplified (3):** at filing/registration you no longer fill in each raw material's safety dossier and submission code — just the manufacturer name; the rest is kept on file by the enterprise. NMPA no longer publishes the submission codes.
- **Shared safety data for similar formulas (4):** within one brand, formula-similar products can use a single representative product's microbial, physicochemical, toxicology and human-safety test reports, with a similarity justification.
- **Broader efficacy-claim methods (5):** except for spot-whitening, sunscreen and anti-hair-loss, brands may choose industry/international standards, technical guides, or validated in-house methods for efficacy claims (with scientific basis).
- **Shared efficacy data (6):** formula-similar products can also share efficacy-claim evaluation data, with equivalence justification.
- **Easier cross-border production-site transfers (7)** and **simplified responsible-person changes (8):** changing your domestic responsible person (境内责任人) now needs only an authorization, a product list and a commitment letter — no outgoing responsible person's consent or court documents.

## The responsible person still matters

The **domestic responsible person (境内责任人)** requirement under CSAR is unchanged for standard registration and filing: a foreign brand must still appoint a China-based entity to lodge filings, monitor adverse events and act as the local contact. What changed is only the *change* procedure (measure 8). Budget for appointing a competent responsible person — it is one of the most consequential choices you make.

## Where this meets your channel decision

These reforms ease the **general-trade and domestic-store** path (full NMPA filing/registration, Chinese labels, a responsible person). They do **not** replace the leaner **1210 cross-border** route: most cosmetics sold through Tmall Global, JD Worldwide or Douyin cross-border still enter under a simplified positive-list regime without full NMPA filing. For a first market test, 1210 remains the lowest-risk start; the 2025–2026 reforms make the *scale-up* to a domestic store materially faster and cheaper.

See our deeper guide on [NMPA filing vs. registration and cross-border vs. general trade](cosmetics-into-china-nmpa.html), the [1210 bonded import model](what-is-1210-bonded-import.html), and [importing via a Hong Kong trading entity](hong-kong-entity-china-import.html) as the importer-of-record alternative to forming a WFOE.

<div class="statcard"><span class="n">5 cities</span><span class="l">GOODSINFINITE bonded-fulfilment network — Tianjin, Shanghai, Ningbo, Guangzhou, Qingdao — for 1–3 day domestic delivery once your product clears</span><span class="src">Source: GOODSINFINITE TRADE LIMITED fulfilment operations</span></div>

## How GOODSINFINITE supports a beauty entry under the new rules

- **Channel sequencing.** We map whether your SKUs should enter via 1210 first or go straight to general trade, and we pre-screen claim language and category (general vs. special) before anything ships.
- **Responsible-person and filing support.** We coordinate the China responsible person, the dossier, and the new China-first-launch or animal-testing-waiver path where your products qualify.
- **Hong Kong importer of record.** GOODSINFINITE TRADE LIMITED imports under bond — no WFOE needed for a first 1210 test.
- **Five-city bonded fulfilment** for 1–3 day domestic delivery, plus Douyin cross-border livestream and RedNote (Xiaohongshu) seeding built for beauty audiences.

> The 2025–2026 reforms reward brands that move fast: launch in China first, lean on the expanded testing waivers, and let the lighter filing regime cut your time-to-shelf. Pair that with a 1210 test to prove demand before you commit to a domestic store.

## FAQ

**Do imported cosmetics still need to be sold in their home country before entering China?** Not for China-first launches. Under NMPA Announcement 2026 No. 70, international new products launching first in China (or simultaneously worldwide) can submit a China-first-launch commitment declaration and skip the proof of overseas sales — previously a one-to-two-month delay.

**Has China banned animal testing for cosmetics?** No blanket ban. Imported general cosmetics have been exempt since May 2021 if conditions are met; the 2026 Announcement extends the waiver to certain special cosmetics (perming, non-oxidative hair dye, physical-cover whitening) and new-ingredient ordinary cosmetics (excluding children's), with conditions. Most special-use and children's products still need toxicology data.

**What changed for imported cosmetics in 2025–2026?** Two documents: the 24-measure Opinion (国药监妆〔2025〕18号, 17 Nov 2025) set direction, and Announcement 2026 No. 70 (effective 29 Jul 2026) delivered eight measures — China-first launch, expanded testing waivers, simplified raw-material data, shared safety/efficacy data, broader efficacy methods, easier responsible-person changes.

**Do I still need a China responsible person?** Yes, the CSAR requirement remains for registration and filing. But changing the responsible person is now simpler — no outgoing consent letter or court documents, just an authorization, product list and commitment letter.

**Does 1210 cross-border still avoid full NMPA filing?** Yes. Cross-border (1210) retail still uses a simplified positive-list regime; the reforms primarily ease the general-trade and domestic-store path. They solve different problems and can be used together.

- National Medical Products Administration (NMPA) — *Announcement on Matters Concerning Cosmetic Registration and Filing* (2026 No. 70), effective 29 July 2026: [nmpa.gov.cn](https://www.nmpa.gov.cn/xxgk/fgwj/gzwj/gzwjhzhp/20260729115807198.html)

- NMPA — Cosmetics Supervision and Administration Regulation (CSAR, 化妆品监督管理条例) and the Administrative Measures for Cosmetics Registration and Filing: [nmpa.gov.cn](https://www.nmpa.gov.cn/)
- Beijing Municipal Medical Products Administration — Q&A on Announcement 2026 No. 70 optimisation measures: [yjj.beijing.gov.cn](https://yjj.beijing.gov.cn/yjj/xxcx/kpxc/hzp36/744107633/index.html)

## Cross-Border E-Commerce in China: Tmall Global Costs
Source: https://www.goods-infinite.com/insights/cross-border-ecommerce-store-economics-china
Published: 2026-10-02 · Cluster: E-commerce Operations

## The platform's take rate is not your cost — traffic is

Cross-border store unit economics is the discipline of measuring what a single order leaves behind once every platform fee, import tax, logistics charge and traffic cost has been deducted — and in China the result surprises most foreign brands: the platform takes about four percent of the order, and demand creation takes twenty to forty.

The market keeps expanding. China's cross-border e-commerce imports reached RMB 570.2 billion in 2025, up 2.7 percent and a record high, all of it consumer goods ([GACC statistics department, June 2026](http://tjs.customs.gov.cn/tjs/2026-06/16/article_2026061616113844507.html)). By the first half of 2026 customs reported 140 million Chinese consumers buying through cross-border platforms, with overseas-warehouse exports up 3.3-fold ([State Council Information Office, July 2026](https://english.scio.gov.cn/pressroom/2026-07/22/content_118612088.html)).

<div class="statcard"><span class="n">140 million</span><span class="l">Chinese consumers who bought through cross-border e-commerce platforms in the first half of 2026 — against RMB 570.2 billion of cross-border e-commerce imports in 2025, up 2.7 percent and a record high</span><span class="src">Source: General Administration of Customs, State Council Information Office press conference, 22 July 2026; GACC statistics department, June 2026</span></div>

A larger market is not a more profitable one. The pool of Chinese online shoppers has stopped growing and the supply of imported brands has not, which pushes the decisive cost line upward every year.

## Breakeven ROAS is the number to set before the store opens

Breakeven ROAS is the minimum return on advertising spend at which a paid order stops destroying cash, and it equals one divided by the contribution margin that survives after every non-advertising cost has been deducted.

Where contribution margin is what is left of the selling price after goods cost, import tax, commission, payment fees, fulfilment and returns, the breakeven ROAS is 1 ÷ that margin. An order keeping 42 percent needs a ROAS of 2.38; traffic returning less is a subsidy from the brand to the consumer.

Returns belong in the same formula, because a refunded order still consumed goods, tax and freight. The adjusted version is 1 ÷ (contribution margin × (1 − return rate)), which at a 42 percent margin and a 15 percent return rate gives 2.80 rather than 2.38 — a 17 percent higher bar on every campaign.

Most foreign brands invert the sequence — set a GMV target, treat advertising as a residual, then discover the store could never clear its breakeven line at the traffic prices its category commands.

## Six cost lines are fixed before you sell anything

A fixed cost line in a Chinese cross-border store is one set by platform rule, tax law or a logistics contract rather than by the brand's own commercial choices, which is why it can be modelled precisely before launch.

- **Platform commission, 2 to 5 percent of sales** by leaf category, plus payment processing of about 1 percent. [Tmall Global's merchant guidance](https://www.tmall.hk/wow/z/import/pegasus-no-head/S43HbztinhJ6JnTdYXW6) states a normal security deposit of RMB 50,000 and an annual technical service fee of RMB 30,000 or RMB 60,000 by top-level category — highest tier when selling across categories, with no annual fee refund policy. Alibaba's own schedule adds an Alipay cross-border transaction fee of roughly 1 percent.
- **Cross-border import tax, 9.1 percent of the transaction price** on a tax-inclusive listing: zero duty plus VAT and consumption tax at 70 percent of the statutory rate, inside the RMB 5,000 single-order and RMB 26,000 annual limits ([GACC tax guidance](http://www.customs.gov.cn/customs/2026-01/13/article_2026041015241877353.html)), the mechanics set out in our [landed-cost walkthrough](https://www.goods-infinite.com/insights/china-import-taxes-landed-cost.html). High-end cosmetics above the consumption-tax threshold reached 23.1 percent in a published customs example.
- **Bonded storage and handling, around 4 percent of a mid-value order** — market rates of RMB 1.5 to 5 per cubic metre per day of storage, RMB 20 to 50 per pallet inbound and RMB 3 to 8 per outbound order including packaging.
- **Returns provision, 15 to 20 percent on average** and above 30 percent in fashion and small appliances.
- **The annual technical service fee is a scale penalty.** RMB 30,000 to 60,000 is three to six points of a RMB 1 million store, and less than a point at RMB 10 million.
- **Agency operation, 5 to 15 percent of GMV**, where a Tmall Partner runs the account ([how TPs are priced and vetted](https://www.goods-infinite.com/insights/tmall-global-tp-partner.html)).

## Demand creation is the line that decides your margin

Demand creation cost is the total a brand spends on paid traffic, content and agency operation to convert a Chinese shopper who is not already searching for its brand, expressed as a percentage of the resulting GMV — and it is the largest line a brand can actually influence.

The structural reason is that the demand pool has stopped growing. CNNIC's 56th Statistical Report put China's online shopping users at 976 million as of June 2025, up 1.09 million in six months — 0.1 percent growth, at 86.9 percent penetration of all internet users ([CNNIC, 56th Statistical Report on China's Internet Development](https://www.cnnic.net.cn/NMediaFile/2025/0730/MAIN1753846666507QEK67ZS9DH.pdf)). The Ministry of Commerce's research institute states the implication plainly: user growth is no longer the industry's main driver ([Economic Daily, February 2026](https://www.ce.cn/cysc/newmain/yc/jsxw/202602/t20260210_2765337.shtml)).

<div class="statcard"><span class="n">976 million</span><span class="l">China's online shopping users as of June 2025, up 1.09 million in six months — 0.1 percent growth, at 86.9 percent penetration of all internet users</span><span class="src">Source: CNNIC, 56th Statistical Report on China's Internet Development (published July 2025)</span></div>

Inside a store this becomes two bidding systems — keyword and Wanxiangtai placements on Alibaba, Qianchuan on Douyin. Agency benchmarks published in 2026 quote Douyin CPM at RMB 20 to 40, cost per completed order at RMB 30 to 80 and blended campaign ROAS at 1:3.5 to 1:4.2, with beauty at 1:4.5 to 1:6; Tmall keyword click prices reported at RMB 2 to 3 in 2025 were reported at RMB 5 to 10 in 2026. Those are directional rather than official statistics, and belong in a model as a range to test against.

An influencer livestream adds a second demand cost: a fixed fee plus 15 to 30 percent of the GMV it generates, which our [livestream agency guide](https://www.goods-infinite.com/insights/china-livestream-agency-foreign-brands.html) treats as a margin decision rather than a marketing expense.

## Where RMB 100 of cross-border GMV actually goes

A cross-border store profit model is an ordered deduction from the price the consumer pays down to the cash the brand keeps, and the order matters because each line is calculated on a different base.

<div class="table-wrap"><table><thead><tr><th>Line</th><th>RMB per RMB 100 of GMV</th><th>Basis</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>Gross merchandise value</td><td>100.0</td><td>Consumer pays, tax-inclusive listing</td></tr>
<tr><td>Cost of goods</td><td>−30.0</td><td>Imported goods at landed cost</td></tr>
<tr><td>Platform commission</td><td>−3.0</td><td>2–5 percent by leaf category</td></tr>
<tr><td>Payment processing</td><td>−1.0</td><td>Alipay cross-border transaction fee</td></tr>
<tr><td>Cross-border import tax</td><td>−9.1</td><td>Zero duty plus 70 percent of statutory VAT</td></tr>
<tr><td>Bonded storage, pick and pack</td><td>−4.0</td><td>Storage, inbound handling, outbound order</td></tr>
<tr><td>Returns and after-sales</td><td>−5.0</td><td>Approximately 15 percent return rate</td></tr>
<tr><td><strong>Contribution before demand creation</strong></td><td><strong>47.9</strong></td><td>52 percent already consumed</td></tr>
<tr><td>Paid traffic and content</td><td>−25.0</td><td>20–30 percent of GMV is normal</td></tr>
<tr><td>Agency or TP operation</td><td>−8.0</td><td>5–15 percent of GMV</td></tr>
<tr><td><strong>Operating contribution</strong></td><td><strong>14.9</strong></td><td>Before salaries, overheads and brand marketing</td></tr>
</tbody></table></div>

### Reading the model

RMB 52 of every RMB 100 is consumed before the brand buys a single advertisement, and only about 30 of the remaining points are genuinely discretionary once store salaries and overheads are funded.

### The two sensitivities that decide the outcome

Two sensitivities decide whether that 14.9 survives. Raise the return rate from 15 to 30 percent — routine in fashion — and the contribution before demand creation falls about 7 points, putting the store at break-even at the same traffic cost. Hold returns and let ad spend reach 35 percent in competitive beauty, and the operating contribution halves.

## What SAMR's platform fee rules let you demand

The Compliance Guide for Network Trading Platform Fee Behaviour is a State Administration for Market Regulation instrument published and effective on 31 July 2025, setting binding expectations on what a Chinese platform may charge the merchants trading on it ([SAMR, July 2025](https://www.samr.gov.cn/xw/zj/art/2025/art_c35be0a9ae514fd9b37bfd3620b678c1.html)).

### The eight prohibited charges

Article 23 prohibits eight categories of unreasonable charge: repeat charging; charging without delivering the service or delivering less than charged for; shifting the platform's own costs onto merchants; charging merchants for access to their own basic operating data; forcing or de facto forcing merchants to buy services or join promotions with a fee; using unreasonable deposits to charge indirectly or raise the fee standard; price discrimination between merchants on equal trading terms; and any other unreasonable charge.

Three further provisions matter to a store budget. Fee schedules, items and amounts must be displayed permanently in a prominent position on the platform homepage. Changes require a public comment period of at least seven days, and a merchant that rejects a change may leave the platform, which may not obstruct it. Promotional cost-sharing ratios must be agreed in advance; without agreement the platform cannot add promotion fees afterwards.

### What a brand can ask for

Article 24 gives the merchant a formal route: a merchant that considers a fee above a reasonable level may raise it with supporting material, and the platform must respond promptly and negotiate — starting with a written request for the current fee schedule and the calculation method behind every click- and conversion-priced charge.

## Store broadcast is the cheapest live-commerce route in China

Store broadcast, or 店播, is live commerce run from a brand's own account rather than through a paid host or influencer, and it is now the majority of China's live-commerce market. The 2025 Live Commerce Industry White Paper, produced by SAMR's Development Research Centre with the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences, put 2025 live-commerce GMV above RMB 5 trillion — around a third of online retail, with 660 million users — and found that brand-operated store broadcast exceeds 50 percent of that total, while top-host GMV share fell to 10.66 percent ([MOFCOM e-commerce portal, February 2026](https://dzswgf.mofcom.gov.cn/news/43/2026/2/1770703142379.html)).

The reason is arithmetic. An influencer session costs 15 to 30 percent of the GMV it generates plus a fixed fee; store broadcast costs content production and paid traffic. Douyin reports more than 80,000 new merchants crossing RMB 1 million of GMV through store broadcast in 2025.

## Modelling the store before you commit

Cross-border store economics is a small number of decisions in a specific order. Set the breakeven ROAS from the margin your category can hold. Treat tax, commission, payment, fulfilment and returns as fixed. Manage advertising, agency and content against that floor, and read traffic cost weekly — it moves faster in China than in any other market a foreign brand is likely to sell in.

GOODSINFINITE TRADE LIMITED acts as importer of record and China import agent for foreign brands, operating bonded cross-border fulfilment from Tianjin, Shanghai, Ningbo, Guangzhou and Qingdao, and building store cost models before a brand commits to a channel. Our [China market entry guide](https://www.goods-infinite.com/guide-china-market-entry.html) places these numbers inside the wider entry sequence, and the [glossary](https://www.goods-infinite.com/glossary.html) defines the platform and customs terms used here.

## FAQ

**Is cross-border e-commerce in China profitable for a foreign brand?** It can be, but not because of the platform's take rate. Commission and payment fees take roughly 4 percent of sales and cross-border import tax takes 9.1 percent on a tax-inclusive listing, so about 52 of every 100 yuan of GMV is consumed by goods, tax, commission, fulfilment and returns before any advertising is bought. Profitability is decided by demand creation, which commonly runs 20 to 30 percent of GMV.

**What is breakeven ROAS and how is it calculated for a China store?** Breakeven ROAS is the minimum return on advertising spend at which a paid order stops losing money: one divided by the contribution margin that survives after every non-advertising cost. Including platform refunds, it becomes one divided by (contribution margin times one minus the return rate). An order keeping 42 percent needs a ROAS of 2.38 at zero returns and about 2.80 at a 15 percent return rate.

**What does Tmall Global actually charge a merchant in 2026?** Tmall Global's merchant guidance lists a security deposit normally of RMB 50,000, refundable on a clean closure; an annual technical service fee of RMB 30,000 or RMB 60,000 by top-level category, with the highest tier applied to stores selling across categories and no annual fee refund policy; and commission of 2 to 5 percent by leaf category. Alibaba's commission schedule adds an Alipay cross-border transaction fee of roughly 1 percent.

**Which costs in a Chinese cross-border store cannot be negotiated?** Six: the cross-border import tax inside the RMB 5,000 single-order and RMB 26,000 annual limits; platform commission; the roughly 1 percent payment fee; bonded storage and per-order handling; the returns provision for your category; and the annual technical service fee. Advertising, agency operation and content are the lines a brand genuinely controls.

**What can a foreign brand do about platform fees in China?** SAMR's Compliance Guide for Network Trading Platform Fee Behaviour, effective 31 July 2025, requires fee schedules and itemised amounts to be permanently displayed on the platform homepage, imposes a public comment period of at least seven days before any change, prohibits charging merchants for access to their own basic operating data, and prohibits promotion fees imposed without prior agreement on cost sharing. Article 24 allows a merchant to raise an allegedly excessive fee with supporting material, obliging the platform to respond and negotiate.

## China Customs Valuation: How Royalties, Assists and Related-Party Prices Set Your Import Tax Base
Source: https://www.goods-infinite.com/insights/china-customs-valuation-royalties
Published: 2026-09-30 · Cluster: Logistics & Distribution

## Your import tax base in China is not the price on the invoice

China customs valuation is the process by which the General Administration of Customs determines the value on which import duty, import VAT and consumption tax are levied on imported goods, and it routinely produces a number higher than the one on the commercial invoice. Since the Tariff Law took effect on 1 December 2024 the concept carries a new name — the taxable price, or 计税价格 — and its rules sit in Articles 24 to 28 of the [Tariff Law](http://www.customs.gov.cn/customs/2024-12/26/article_2025121221030676770.html) and in the [GACC Measures for Determining the Taxable Price of Imported and Exported Goods](http://www.customs.gov.cn/customs/2021-12/21/article_2026010416440399917.html), Order No. 213 of 2013 as amended by Order No. 273 of 2024.

Where the importer buys from a related overseas seller, or pays a trademark or know-how royalty, the base becomes a position customs can challenge for three years.

<div class="statcard"><span class="n">3 years</span><span class="l">How far back customs can recover under-collected duty where the importer's own non-compliance caused it, charged at 0.05 percent per day in late fees — about 18 percent a year, running from the date of release rather than the date of discovery</span><span class="src">Source: Tariff Law of the People's Republic of China, effective 1 December 2024, Articles 46 and 47</span></div>

## The base starts with transaction value, then additions and deductions

Transaction value is the price actually paid or payable for goods sold for export to China, adjusted by the additions and deductions the law mandates, and it is the compulsory starting point for every valuation. Article 24 of the Tariff Law adds freight and insurance up to the place of arrival, so a CIF price is effectively complete while FOB and CFR prices are not. Only where the transaction value fails the statutory conditions does customs move to five alternative methods — identical goods, similar goods, deductive value, computed value and reasonable means — after a formal price consultation.

<div class="table-wrap"><table><thead><tr><th>Treatment</th><th>Item</th><th>What to watch</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>Added</td><td>Commissions and brokerage borne by the buyer</td><td>Buying commission is excluded — the only commission that is</td></tr>
<tr><td>Added</td><td>Containers, packing materials and packing labour</td><td>Applies where they are treated as one with the goods</td></tr>
<tr><td>Added</td><td>Assists: materials, components, tools, dies, moulds, consumables, and design or development work done abroad</td><td>The most frequently missed category; the value must be apportioned to the shipment</td></tr>
<tr><td>Added</td><td>Royalties related to the goods that are a condition of their sale</td><td>Both tests must be satisfied, not one</td></tr>
<tr><td>Added</td><td>Proceeds of resale, disposal or use that accrue to the seller</td><td>Common in consignment and profit-share terms</td></tr>
<tr><td>Deducted</td><td>Post-import construction, installation, assembly, maintenance and technical assistance</td><td>Warranty costs are expressly not deductible</td></tr>
<tr><td>Deducted</td><td>Freight and insurance arising after arrival in China</td><td>Only the pre-arrival leg belongs in the base</td></tr>
<tr><td>Deducted</td><td>Import duty and domestic taxes</td><td>Must be separately itemised on the invoice to be excluded</td></tr>
<tr><td>Deducted</td><td>Cost of reproducing the goods in China, plus Chinese technical training and overseas inspection visits</td><td>Routinely overlooked credits</td></tr>
<tr><td>Deducted</td><td>Interest on a financed purchase</td><td>Four conditions: genuine purchase financing, a written facility agreement, interest separately stated, and a rate no higher than the market rate for comparable transactions</td></tr>
</tbody></table></div>

## A royalty is dutiable on two tests, not on what the contract calls it

A royalty is dutiable in China only where it is related to the imported goods and its payment is a condition of their sale into China, so the two must be tested separately. Article 25 of the Tariff Law brings into the base royalties the buyer must pay, directly or indirectly, to the seller or a related party as a condition of the sale, and the Measures define when each limb is met.

The relationship test in Article 13 recognises four categories. A patent or know-how royalty is related where the goods contain it, are produced by it, or were specially designed to implement it. A trademark royalty is related where the goods bear the mark, can be sold once it is attached, or can be sold after light processing with the mark attached; copyright and distribution or sales-rights royalties cover goods containing software, text, music or images, and goods sellable directly or after light processing. Light processing means dilution, mixing, sorting, simple assembly, repackaging or comparable operations — not a change in physical or chemical character. The condition test in Article 14 is met where the buyer cannot obtain the goods, or cannot obtain them on the agreed terms, without paying the royalty.

Applied together, the tests surprise brands. A Chinese pharmaceutical importer paying a trademark royalty on finished medicines — where the imported goods were raw material and the mark was attached only to the finished product — falls outside the base, while the process know-how fee on the same contract fell inside it, because the know-how could only be implemented using that imported raw material ([Tianjin municipal trade bureau, worked customs case](https://shangwuju.tj.gov.cn/tjsswjzz/ztzl/ztzl/swfzjsgz1/gpmy/hyzc/202205/t20220517_5883320.html)). The same reasoning separates an engine from a car: buy branded engines and assemble cars in China, and the engine royalty is dutiable while the car trademark royalty is not.

## A special relationship does not disqualify your price — it moves the burden onto you

A special relationship in Chinese customs valuation is a defined family, control or ownership link between buyer and seller that places the transaction value under scrutiny rather than automatically replacing it. Article 16 of the Measures lists eight situations, including family ties, officer or director overlap, common control by a third party, and ownership or control of five percent or more of the other party's publicly issued voting shares; a sole agency, distributorship or concession arrangement qualifies where it meets any of those tests.

The consequence is procedural, not fatal. Article 8 permits the transaction value of related parties provided the relationship did not influence the price, and Article 17 sets out how that is proved: if the declared price is close to sales of identical or similar goods to unrelated buyers in China, or to a deductive or computed value, the relationship is deemed not to have affected it.

No numerical tolerance for "close" exists in the rules, which turns an intercompany price into a position needing evidence — a comparables file, a transfer-pricing study, or an advance ruling. Where the defence cannot be made, customs rejects the transaction value and works down the Article 6 hierarchy, which is how a related-party import ends up taxed on the Chinese resale price.

<div class="statcard"><span class="n">5 percent</span><span class="l">The equity threshold at which buyer and seller are deemed specially related in Chinese customs valuation — one of eight listed situations, alongside family ties, common control and officer or director overlap</span><span class="src">Source: GACC Measures for Determining the Taxable Price of Imported and Exported Goods (Order No. 213, as amended by Order No. 273, effective 1 December 2024), Article 16</span></div>

## A royalty paid after import has its own 30-day clock

Subsequent royalty declaration is the procedure for paying import tax on a dutiable royalty not settled when the goods were imported, and it runs on a separate timeline. Under [GACC Announcement No. 58 of 2019](https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2019-11/05/content_5448785.htm), the importer must answer the royalty confirmation field on every declaration — exports, processing trade and bonded goods other than those sold domestically are exempt — and where a dutiable royalty was already paid at import, the amount goes in the incidental charges field rather than the total price.

Where it has not been paid, the royalty must be declared within 30 days of each payment, using a dedicated form and supervision code 9500 for subsequent royalty taxation, with the commodity description and code copied from the original import declaration. Failing to complete the confirmation field at all attracts a late fee of 0.05 percent per day from release until the violation is discovered.

Enforcement is routine. A Ningbo company importing throttle sensors, motors and iron cores from Indonesia and Thailand between 2021 and 2024, paying a technology transfer fee and variable technical royalties to its Japanese parent, was ordered to pay the undeclared duties ([China Customs journal, 2025](https://chinacustoms.gmcmonline.com/202502/c/20786.shtml)). Two Sichuan cases show the range of outcomes: 27 consignments where the confirmation field was left blank drew a fine of about RMB 30,000 for affecting customs supervision order, while royalties paid without the 30-day declaration drew RMB 100,000 for affecting tax collection ([Sichuan digital trade portal, customs guidance](https://www.tradesichuan.com/jmzx/2264.html)). The procedural omission is cheaper than the fiscal one, and neither is as cheap as disclosure.

## Voluntary disclosure is the cheapest exit from a past under-declaration

Voluntary disclosure is a Chinese customs compliance mechanism under which an enterprise that reports its own violation before customs finds it can avoid administrative penalty and have late fees reduced or waived. The instrument in force is the GACC announcement on handling voluntary disclosure, [published 28 September 2025 and effective from 11 October 2025 to 30 June 2027](https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202509/P020260317144837336887.pdf), which replaced the 2023 announcement.

No penalty applies where the disclosure is made within six months of the violation, or between six and twenty-four months where the underpaid tax is no more than 30 percent of the tax payable or no more than RMB 1 million. And a disclosure resulting in a warning or a fine of up to RMB 1 million is not entered in the enterprise's customs credit record — a distinction that matters to any brand watching its importer of record's rating.

Customs has published worked illustrations. A company that had under-declared royalties on imports made between January and May, with roughly RMB 1.3 million of tax underpaid against about RMB 5 million paid on those consignments, was confirmed as penalty-free because the shortfall was around 20 percent — inside the 30 percent threshold ([GACC Customs Policy Express, January 2026](http://www.customs.gov.cn/customs/2026-01/13/article_2026041015241473300.html)).

<div class="statcard"><span class="n">RMB 1.3M</span><span class="l">Royalties under-declared by one importer, against roughly RMB 5 million of tax paid on the same consignments — a 20 percent shortfall, inside the 30 percent threshold that qualifies a disclosure made within two years for no penalty</span><span class="src">Source: General Administration of Customs, Customs Policy Express briefing, published January 2026</span></div>

## Certainty before you import: the valuation advance ruling

An advance ruling is a binding written decision customs issues before the goods are imported, covering the valuation elements or the valuation method to be applied, and it is available to foreign brands as well as Chinese importers. Article 10 of the [Measures for the Administration of the Collection of Import and Export Duties](http://www.customs.gov.cn/customs/fileDir/resource/cms/article/302267/6176833/2024102908485851207.pdf), GACC Order No. 272, effective 1 December 2024, confirms that customs may rule in advance on the elements or method of determining the taxable price, on classification and on origin. A ruling is issued within 60 days of acceptance and remains valid for three years. The same regulation allows a supplementary declaration to be requested by the importer.

For a brand with a substantial royalty stream or an intercompany price above the transfer-pricing radar, an advance ruling converts the largest single uncertainty in the cost model into a fixed number. It must be applied for at least three months before the first import.

## What this means for a foreign brand's structure

Customs valuation is the one part of a China import model where the price is not simply what the supplier invoices. Every structure that crosses a border between related entities, or pays separately for a brand or a technology, creates a base customs can test — and the tests run on documents that exist only if they were created deliberately: the licence agreement, the assist apportionment, the comparables file behind an intercompany price, and the confirmation field on every declaration.

GOODSINFINITE TRADE LIMITED acts as importer of record and China import agent for foreign brands, handling royalty declaration, supplementary declarations and advance-ruling applications through bonded and general-trade channels in Tianjin, Shanghai, Ningbo, Guangzhou and Qingdao. Our [China market entry guide](https://www.goods-infinite.com/guide-china-market-entry.html) places valuation inside the wider compliance sequence, and the [glossary](https://www.goods-infinite.com/glossary.html) defines the terms used here.

## FAQ

**How is the customs value of imported goods determined in China?** By the transaction value first — the price actually paid or payable when the goods are sold for export to China — adjusted for the statutory additions and deductions. Since 1 December 2024 the concept is called the taxable price (计税价格), governed by Articles 24 to 28 of the Tariff Law and the GACC Measures. Only where the transaction value fails the statutory conditions does customs move through the five alternative methods, from identical goods to a reasonable-means valuation.

**Are royalties always added to the customs value in China?** No. A royalty is dutiable only where it relates to the imported goods and its payment is a condition of their sale into China. The rules define four categories of relationship — patents and technical know-how, trademarks, copyright, and distribution or sales rights — and treat payment as a condition where the buyer cannot obtain the goods, or cannot obtain them on the agreed contract terms, without paying it.

**Can an importer still use the invoice price when buyer and seller are related?** Yes, if it can show the relationship did not affect the price. Eight situations create a special relationship, including a five percent equity link and common control, but the rules provide a defence: where the price is close to sales of identical or similar goods to unrelated buyers in China, or to a deductive or computed value, the relationship is deemed not to have influenced it. If no benchmark can be met, the transaction value is rejected.

**What happens when a royalty is paid after the goods have been imported?** It has its own declaration window. Where a dutiable royalty was not paid at import, the importer must declare it within 30 days of each payment under GACC Announcement No. 58 of 2019, using supervision code 9500, and pays at the rate and exchange rate in force on the date customs accepts the royalty declaration rather than the original import date.

**What is voluntary disclosure in Chinese customs, and what does it cost?** A mechanism allowing an enterprise that reports its own violation before customs finds it to avoid administrative penalty and have late fees reduced or waived. Under the announcement in force since 11 October 2025, no penalty applies to a disclosure made within six months, or between six months and two years where the underpaid tax is no more than 30 percent of the tax payable or no more than RMB 1 million. A resulting fine of up to RMB 1 million is not recorded in the enterprise's customs credit file.

## Do You Need GACC Registration to Import Food Into China? (Decree 248)
Source: https://www.goods-infinite.com/insights/do-you-need-gacc-registration
Published: 2026-09-29 · Cluster: Compliance & Registration

## Definition: what "GACC registration" actually means for imported food

"GACC registration" is the pre-clearance that the **General Administration of Customs of China (GACC)** requires an **overseas food manufacturer** to hold before its products can be exported to mainland China. It is not a brand-level licence and not an importer licence — it is the factory's permission to export. Under **GACC Decree 248** (《进口食品境外生产企业注册管理规定》), in force since **1 January 2022**, nearly every overseas plant that makes, processes, or stores food for China must be on GACC's register ([GACC](https://www.customs.gov.cn)).

<div class="statcard"><span class="n">18 categories</span><span class="l">of imported food require GACC overseas-manufacturer registration via official recommendation by the home-country authority</span><span class="src">Source: GACC Decree 248 (Art. 7), effective 2022-01-01</span></div>

The single most useful reframing for a new brand: **"Do I need GACC registration?" is the wrong question.** The right question is **"Is my product in the 18 categories that need the heavier registration, or in the self-registration path?"** — and, in either case, **"Is my China importer properly record-filed?"**

## The legal baseline: Decree 248 and who must register

GACC Decree 248 consolidated a patchwork of rules into one framework and shifted the burden onto the overseas manufacturer:

- **Every overseas food manufacturer, processor, or storage facility** exporting food to China must be registered with GACC ([GACC Announcement 2021 No. 103](https://www.customs.gov.cn)).
- **Article 7 — 18 categories** require registration through **official recommendation** (官方推荐注册) by the exporting country's competent food-safety authority, then review by GACC.
- **Article 9 — everything else** is registered by the manufacturer directly through the **self-registration** (企业自主申请) path.
- A registered **China import entity** (进口商备案) is still required to lodge each shipment and share food-safety accountability — this is separate from the manufacturer registration ([GACC](https://www.customs.gov.cn)).

> If your plant is not on the GACC register, your goods are refused at the border — regardless of Chinese demand.

## The 18 categories that require official-recommendation registration

If your SKU sits in one of these, GACC registration via your home-country competent authority is non-negotiable ([GACC Announcement 2021 No. 103](https://www.customs.gov.cn)):

| # | Category | # | Category |
|---|----------|---|----------|
| 1 | Meat and meat products | 10 | Edible grains |
| 2 | Sausage casings | 11 | Milled-grain products & malt |
| 3 | Aquatic products | 12 | Fresh & dehydrated vegetables, dried beans |
| 4 | Dairy products | 13 | Condiments |
| 5 | Bird's nests & nest products | 14 | Nuts and seeds |
| 6 | Bee products | 15 | Dried fruits |
| 7 | Eggs and egg products | 16 | Unroasted coffee beans & cocoa beans |
| 8 | Edible oils and oilseeds | 17 | Foods for special dietary purposes* |
| 9 | Stuffed wheaten products | 18 | Health food (保健食品) |

\* Includes infant formula and foods for special medical purpose. This is the representative list issued by GACC via its customs Q&A and Announcement 103; always confirm your HS code in the CIFER system's product-category query before shipping.

## The decision tree: do *you* need GACC registration?

Follow this in order:

1. **Are you the overseas manufacturer / processor / storage site?** If you make food for the China market, you must register (Decree 248 applies to the plant, not the brand). If you only distribute, you are the importer — go to step 4.
2. **Is your product in the 18 Article-7 categories?** → Yes: your home-country competent authority recommends you to GACC; GACC reviews and issues an 18-digit China Registration Number. → No: you self-register directly through CIFER.
3. **Is your registration in force?** Valid registrations are renewed by applying **3–6 months before expiry**; GACC extends validity by **5 years** on renewal ([People's Daily / Ningbo Customs Q&A](https://www.customs.gov.cn)).
4. **Is your China importer record-filed (进口商备案)?** This is required for **every** shipment, on top of the manufacturer registration. Without a record-filed importer, customs will not accept the declaration.

## How registration actually works (and what it costs)

- **The only official portal is CIFER** — the China Import Food Enterprises Registration System at [cifer.singlewindow.cn](https://cifer.singlewindow.cn). GACC states this is the sole official platform and that **registration is free of charge** ([GACC notice](https://www.customs.gov.cn)).
- **For the 18 categories**, the home-country competent authority is allocated a CIFER account by GACC, audits the plant, and submits the recommendation; the manufacturer then completes the dossier in the system.
- **For other foods**, the manufacturer (or its agent) opens its own CIFER account and submits directly.
- **On approval**, GACC issues an **18-digit China Registration Number (在华注册编号)** that must be printed on **both the inner and outer packaging** of the exported food (Decree 248, Art. 15) ([GACC FAQ](https://www.customs.gov.cn)).
- At import declaration, the number is entered under "product qualification" (licence category code 519); mis-reporting means customs rejects the declaration ([GACC Announcement 2021 No. 103](https://www.customs.gov.cn)).

## Where the China importer of record fits

A foreign brand rarely files anything itself. The practical chain is:

- **Overseas manufacturer** → registered with GACC (steps above).
- **China importer of record** → holds import record-filing, lodges the declaration, matches each shipment to a valid manufacturer number, handles labelling review and tax.
- **Hong Kong trading arm** (optional) → acts as overseas shipper, title holder and FX layer, working *with* a China-side import operation. See [using a Hong Kong entity to import into China](hong-kong-entity-china-import.html).

Our deeper walkthrough of the dossier, documents, and timelines is in [GACC registration for imported food: a step-by-step guide](gacc-food-registration.html).

## Common mistakes that get food rejected

- **Assuming all food is treated equally.** Treating an Article-7 category as a self-registration leads to a refused shipment.
- **Starting registration after platform onboarding.** The 18-category path can take months; run it in parallel with Tmall Global / JD Worldwide setup.
- **Skipping the home-country recommendation.** For the 18 categories, your national food-safety authority must recommend the plant — brands that omit this stall.
- **Forgetting the importer record-filing.** Manufacturer registration is necessary but not sufficient; the shipment still needs a record-filed China importer.
- **Missing the packaging number.** The 18-digit China Registration Number must be on inner and outer packaging before export.

## FAQ

**Do I need GACC registration to import food into China?** If your overseas factory makes one of 18 specific food categories, the site must be registered with GACC before export. For all other foods the manufacturer still registers, through a lighter self-registration path. Separately, a China import entity must hold importer record-filing for every shipment.

**Which foods require GACC registration?** Decree 248 Article 7 lists 18 categories requiring registration via official recommendation: meat and meat products, sausage casings, aquatic products, dairy, bird's nests, bee products, eggs, edible oils and oilseeds, stuffed wheaten products, edible grains, milled-grain products and malt, fresh and dehydrated vegetables and dried beans, condiments, nuts and seeds, dried fruits, unroasted coffee beans and cocoa beans, foods for special dietary purposes, and health food.

**What is the difference between official-recommendation registration and self-registration?** The 18 Article-7 categories are recommended by the overseas country's competent authority and reviewed by GACC. Foods outside those 18 are registered directly by the manufacturer through CIFER without a government recommendation. Both yield an 18-digit China Registration Number; the difference is who initiates and the depth of review.

**How do I register, and does it cost anything?** Registration is done only through the official CIFER portal (cifer.singlewindow.cn). GACC confirms it is the sole official platform and that registration is free of charge. For the 18 categories the application is submitted by the home-country competent authority; for other foods the manufacturer self-registers.

**Can a foreign brand without a China company register and import?** The overseas manufacturer is the registrant of record, but a record-filed China import entity must lodge each shipment. A brand without a mainland company can import through a licensed importer of record or a Hong Kong trading entity working with a China-side import operation.
