## China Market Entry Through Offline Retail: Department Stores, Clubs and Convenience Chains
Source: https://www.goods-infinite.com/insights/china-market-entry-offline-retail-channels
Published: 2026-09-18 · Cluster: Market Research

## What offline retail means in the China market

Offline retail in China is the set of physical store formats — supermarkets, membership warehouse clubs, convenience chains, department stores and pharmacies — through which packaged goods reach consumers without a cross-border e-commerce parcel, and it still takes the large majority of Chinese consumer spending. In 2025 total retail sales of consumer goods reached RMB 50,120.2 billion, up 3.7 percent year on year, of which online physical-goods sales were RMB 13,092.3 billion, or 26.1 percent of the total ([National Bureau of Statistics, December 2025 release](https://www.stats.gov.cn/english/PressRelease/202601/t20260120_1962354.html)).

<div class="statcard"><span class="n">73.9%</span><span class="l">Share of China's RMB 50.1 trillion retail market still transacted through physical stores in 2025 — online physical-goods sales accounted for only 26.1%</span><span class="src">Source: National Bureau of Statistics, Total Retail Sales of Consumer Goods in December 2025, published January 2026</span></div>

The more useful signal sits inside that share. By retail format across above-designated-size operators, 2025 growth was uneven ([NBS, same release](https://www.stats.gov.cn/english/PressRelease/202601/t20260120_1962354.html)):

- Convenience stores: **+5.5 percent** — the fastest-growing large format.
- Supermarkets: **+4.3 percent** — still the volume engine for packaged food and daily goods.
- Specialty stores: **+2.6 percent**.
- Department stores: **+0.1 percent** — flat, and now a brand-building channel rather than a volume one.
- Brand-exclusive stores: **−0.6 percent** — the only format that shrank.

## The six places an imported product can actually sit

A China retail channel is a specific store format with its own buying office, listing terms and shopper mission, and the format you choose decides your margin, your pack sizes and how much marketing you will be asked to fund.

<div class="table-wrap"><table>
<thead><tr><th>Channel</th><th>Representative operators</th><th>Why it matters</th><th>Entry reality</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td>Membership warehouse clubs</td><td>Sam's Club, Costco, Metro PLUS</td><td>Single largest route to middle-class households for imported food, homeware and nutrition</td><td>Hard negotiation on price and pack size; buyers expect a 20–30% advantage over comparable supermarket pricing</td></tr>
<tr><td>Supermarkets and premium grocery</td><td>Ole', Yonghui, RT-Mart, Hema Fresh, ALDI</td><td>National volume plus a steady promotion calendar</td><td>Margin, listing support and central-warehouse delivery capability decide it</td></tr>
<tr><td>Convenience chains</td><td>Meiyijia, Easyjoy, Kunlun Haoke, 7-Eleven, Lawson</td><td>Fastest-growing format; one listing decision reaches thousands of points of sale</td><td>Single-serve impulse price points; small pack formats and long shelf life</td></tr>
<tr><td>Department stores and beauty specialty</td><td>SKP, Inzone, Watsons, Sephora</td><td>Counter-based distribution for beauty and fragrance</td><td>Brand-owned fixtures and beauty-advisor staffing</td></tr>
<tr><td>Pharmacy chains</td><td>Regional drugstore chains</td><td>The only counter where registered health-food claims are legal</td><td>Requires the health-food registration certificate</td></tr>
<tr><td>Instant retail overlay</td><td>Meituan, JD, Taobao instant channels</td><td>Turns a physical listing into an online listing within a 30-minute radius</td><td>Shelf presence or a cloud warehouse, plus retailer stock feeds</td></tr>
</tbody></table></div>

Scale is concentrated. Sam's Club reached 63 stores by the end of April 2026 and 67 by mid-May, on 2025 sales above RMB 140 billion with more than 10.7 million paying members, while Costco still operates seven mainland stores ([21st Century Business Herald, May 2026](https://www.21jingji.com/article/20260527/herald/6d8b9e4cbd349a4cced153962d141c32.html)). Convenience is more fragmented but far larger in store count: the top 100 chains operated 208,000 stores at the end of 2025, up 5.6 percent, led by Meiyijia with 40,147 ([China Chain Store & Franchise Association, 2026 China Convenience Store Top 100](https://www.china.com.cn/aboutus/2026-08/04/content_118632936.htm)). The overlay channel is growing fastest — instant retail reached RMB 971.4 billion in 2025, up from RMB 781 billion in 2024, and is forecast to pass RMB 1 trillion in 2026 ([MOFCOM Research Institute, Instant Retail Development Report 2025](https://www.ce.cn/cysc/zljd/gd/202603/t20260319_2838062.shtml)) — so a shelf decision is now also an online availability decision.

## Why cross-border goods cannot simply be put on a shelf

A cross-border e-commerce retail import is a parcel sold to an individual consumer for personal use under China's cross-border retail framework — and under the joint notice that governs it, that parcel may not be resold. The notice, issued jointly by MOFCOM, customs, tax and market-regulation authorities, limits goods bought through the cross-border retail channel to personal use and prohibits resale ([GACC policy briefing confirming Shangfa Cai Fa No. 486 of 2018](http://www.customs.gov.cn/customs/2026-01/13/article_2026041015241860378.html)). Two consequences follow:

- **Bonded goods cannot be routed into stores.** In principle a bonded import may not operate an online-bonded-plus-offline-self-pickup model outside a customs supervision zone, so the warehouse-to-shelf shortcut does not exist.
- **The retail limits stay with the consumer.** RMB 5,000 per order and RMB 26,000 a year apply per individual.

Shelf presence therefore means general trade (customs code 0110): duty and 13 percent import VAT paid up front, a Chinese-language label meeting the mandatory standard for the category, category registration or filing where required, and a mainland supplier on the invoice. Our comparison of [1210, 9610 and 0110](https://www.goods-infinite.com/insights/1210-vs-9610-vs-0110.html), the [labelling requirements](https://www.goods-infinite.com/insights/china-import-product-labelling-requirements.html) and the [landed-cost walkthrough](https://www.goods-infinite.com/insights/china-import-taxes-landed-cost.html) cover each of those steps.

## What a Chinese category buyer asks for before listing

A listing pack is the document set a retailer's category buyer reviews before approving a new SKU for the shelf, and it is where most first listings stall. Buyers across formats now ask for broadly the same file:

- **Supplier qualification:** a mainland-registered entity with import and export rights, a food business licence where food is involved, and the ability to issue a 13 percent VAT special invoice.
- **Lot documentation:** the customs declaration, inspection and quarantine certificate and tax-payment certificate — evidence that the goods entered under general trade, not cross-border retail.
- **Product compliance:** Chinese label artwork in the mandatory format (GB 7718 for prepackaged food, GB 18401 and GB 31701 for textiles), GB test reports, a registration or filing certificate for regulated categories, and enough remaining shelf life — two-thirds of labelled life at delivery is a common minimum.
- **Brand chain of title:** a China trademark registration certificate or an authorised-distribution letter.
- **Barcode and article master data:** a GS1-compliant retail barcode mapped into the retailer's article master — imported goods may use the overseas manufacturer's registered code, but goods produced in China under a foreign-registered code must be filed with the national barcode technical body.
- **Commercial and marketing support:** ex-warehouse supply price, front margin, annual rebate, delivery into the regional distribution centre, returns terms, and sampling or in-store demonstration support.

## The commercial terms — and the rules that cap them

A retail listing agreement in China is a contract between a retailer and a supplier covering supply price, margin, payment terms, promotional contributions and returns, and two instruments set the boundaries — one binding since 2006, one published in May 2026. The binding one is the Fair Trading Measures between Retailers and Suppliers (Order No. 17 of 2006, issued by MOFCOM with the NDRC, the Ministry of Public Security, the State Taxation Administration and SAIC) ([full text, MOFCOM](https://sczxs.mofcom.gov.cn/article/cbw/ddfg/ag/201208/20120808294156.shtml)):

- **Payment terms are capped at 60 days.** Article 14 requires the period to be agreed in the contract and states that it may not exceed 60 days from receipt of the goods; retailers may not delay payment because one product line missed its target or a renewal is pending.
- **Most listing fees have limits.** Charges for signing or renewing a contract, barcode fees, and festival or store-anniversary fees where no service is provided are prohibited; a promotional service fee must be agreed in advance, matched to a service actually performed, invoiced and taxed.
- **Your pricing and customer base are yours.** A retailer may not restrict the prices at which you sell to consumers or other operators, nor restrict your supply to other retailers.
- **Staff and returns are negotiable.** A retailer may not require you to send staff into its stores unless you agree and they work only on your goods, with the cost borne by the retailer where the arrangement is its requirement; you may also refuse returns caused by the retailer's own handling.

The May 2026 instrument is softer but increasingly cited in negotiations: the Domestic Trade Transaction Guidelines (trial), issued by 17 national industry associations and chambers under the guidance of MOFCOM, the NDRC, the Ministry of Justice and the Cyberspace Administration ([International Business Daily summary](https://sw.wuhan.gov.cn/xwdt/mtbd/202605/t20260513_2763928.shtml)). Across seven chapters and 38 articles it recommends payment within 30 days of delivery and no longer than 60, requires overdue interest referenced to the one-year loan prime rate, bars buyers from conditioning payment on matters outside their control such as "waiting for a third party to pay", forbids forcing smaller suppliers to accept commercial bills or accounts-receivable vouchers instead of cash, sets a seven-day acceptance window from delivery, and states that promotions must comply with Order No. 17 and may not be imposed on suppliers without agreement.

One fee changed by name in 2026. Under the revised Commodity Barcode Measures, in force since 1 May 2026, sellers may not charge suppliers entry fees, shelf-placement fees or information-processing fees in the name of product barcodes ([SAMR amendment to the Commodity Barcode Measures, gov.cn](https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/2026/issue_12786/202606/content_7071608.html)).

## How to sequence an offline launch

An offline launch plan is a reverse-scheduled sequence that starts from the retailer's buying calendar, and a first listing typically takes six to nine months:

1. **Months 0–2 — settle the route.** Confirm general-trade entry, appoint the importer of record, confirm the registration or filing path for the category, and file the China trademark if it is not already registered.
2. **Months 2–4 — build the listing pack.** Label artwork and printing, plus GB-standard testing. This is where timelines slip, because artwork revisions cascade.
3. **Months 4–6 — reach the buyer.** Clubs buy through regional offices, supermarkets and convenience chains through national or regional category buyers; China International Import Expo in Shanghai each November, SIAL China and FHC Shanghai are the most efficient rooms for those conversations.
4. **Months 6–9 — terms, delivery, rollout.** Negotiate against the rules above, deliver into the distribution centre, and launch two or three highest-velocity SKUs rather than the full range.

## FAQ

**Can I sell cross-border e-commerce goods in a physical store in China?** No. Under Shangfa Cai Fa No. 486 of 2018, goods bought through the cross-border retail channel are for personal use only and may not be resold, and bonded imports in principle may not operate an online-bonded-plus-offline-self-pickup model outside a customs supervision zone. A shelf presence requires general-trade import, duty paid, and any category registration completed.

**How quickly must a Chinese retailer pay a foreign supplier?** Article 14 of the Fair Trading Measures between Retailers and Suppliers caps the agreed payment period at 60 days from receipt of the goods and blocks delay on grounds such as a product line missing its target. The May 2026 Domestic Trade Transaction Guidelines recommend 30 days, cap terms at 60 days, and require overdue interest referenced to the one-year loan prime rate.

**Which listing fees can a Chinese retailer legally charge?** A promotional service fee agreed in advance and matched to a service actually provided — in-store promotion, advertising, posters — is lawful if it is contracted, invoiced and taxed. Fees for signing or renewing a contract, barcode fees, and festival or store-anniversary fees where no service is provided are prohibited, and the revised Commodity Barcode Measures ban entry, shelf-placement and information-processing fees charged in the name of barcodes.

**Can a Chinese retailer control my retail price or stop me supplying other retailers?** No. Article 7 of Order No. 17 prohibits a retailer from restricting the prices at which you sell to consumers or other operators and from restricting your supply to other retailers. A retailer also cannot require you to send staff into its stores unless you agree and they work only on your goods, with the cost borne by the retailer where the arrangement is its requirement.

**Do I need a Chinese entity to get listed offline?** You need a mainland-registered supplier that can hold the import and registration documents and issue a 13 percent VAT special invoice. That can be your own WFOE or a contracted importer or distributor acting as supplier of record, and the goods must enter under general trade with a compliant Chinese-language label.

## China HS Code Classification for Importers: How Your Tariff Line Is Set — and Made Binding
Source: https://www.goods-infinite.com/insights/china-hs-code-classification-importers
Published: 2026-09-16 · Cluster: Logistics & Distribution

## What commodity classification is, and why it is a pricing decision

Commodity classification in China is the act of matching an imported or exported good to its tariff line — the 10-digit code in the country's import tariff schedule — under the rules of the World Customs Organization's Harmonized System convention, and it determines far more than a duty rate. Your code decides the customs duty rate, whether any of the 15 consumption-tax categories apply, which import licences and inspection-and-quarantine requirements attach, and how post-clearance audits read your history. Most foreign brands treat the code as a technicality their broker fills in; in practice it is a commercial variable, because one misapplied heading can add ten percentage points of duty or pull a product into the excise list. Getting it settled before the first container — and getting it settled in writing — is one of the highest-return compliance moves available.

<div class="statcard"><span class="n">3 years</span><span class="l">Validity of a China customs advance ruling on HS classification — after which it can be renewed for a further three years on application</span><span class="src">Source: GACC Order No. 236, Provisional Measures on Advance Ruling Administration (Art. 13), read with GACC Announcement No. 32 of 2024 on renewal</span></div>

## The legal framework: how your code is actually determined

Commodity classification in China is governed by the Provisions on the Administration of Commodity Classification of Import and Export Goods, issued as General Administration of Customs (GACC) Order No. 252, in force since 1 November 2021 and amended by Order No. 273 in October 2024 to sit under the new Tariff Law. The framework is layered, and every layer is checkable before you ship:

- **The tariff schedule.** The 2026 Import Tariff contains 8,972 tariff lines, each carrying MFN, agreement, special-preferential, provisional and general rates side by side ([GACC interpretation of the 2026 Tariff Adjustment Plan](http://www.customs.gov.cn/customs/2025-12/31/article_2025123119401553789.html)).
- **The six General Rules of Interpretation (GRI)**, plus section notes, chapter notes, subheading notes and China's own national subheading notes. Classification proceeds through them in order — GRI 1 classifies by the heading text and notes; later rules resolve multiples, mixtures and unlisted goods.
- **Published precedent.** GACC's administrative rulings and classification decisions on classification are part of the determination base itself, so a prior published answer for your product is not a hint — it is law.
- **Standards as reference.** Relevant national and industry standards may be used as a reference for classification, which matters for materials and performance-driven categories ([Provisions, Art. 2](http://gec.customs.gov.cn/eportal/fileDir/customs/resource/cms/2023/02/2023022310341389439.pdf)).

One timing rule catches importers out: classification follows the **actual state of the goods at the time of declaration**. Goods declared in advance — increasingly common for speed — are classified per their actual state when they arrive at the customs supervision zone, so a product that changes state in transit (assembly, dilution, retail packing) changes code ([Provisions, Art. 5](http://sjs.customs.gov.cn/customs/attachDir/2026/01/2026010615113818740.pdf)).

## Why classification is where imports go wrong

A classification error in China is not a private mistake between you and your broker; it is a declared statement customs can audit, challenge and penalise. The failure modes compound:

1. **Tax drift.** Duty is line-specific, and consumption tax attaches to headings and unit-value thresholds. The same cosmetic can carry 0 or 15 percent consumption tax depending on where it classifies and how it is priced per millilitre.
2. **Licence and inspection exposure.** The code determines whether an import licence, registration or statutory inspection applies — see our walkthrough of [prohibited and restricted goods](https://www.goods-infinite.com/insights/prohibited-restricted-goods-china.html).
3. **Testing and supplementary declaration.** While reviewing a classification, customs may inspect and copy documents, require samples and Chinese translations of technical literature, organise laboratory testing, and ask for a supplementary declaration ([Provisions, Arts. 8–9](http://www.customs.gov.cn/customs/2026-07/30/article_2026073010485045874.html)). Lab tests take weeks and hold the goods.
4. **Penalties.** Where customs determines the declaration was wrong, it re-assesses duty, charges late-payment surcharges, and can penalise misdeclaration under the Implementing Regulations on Customs Administrative Penalties — up to three times the evaded duty — with deliberate misclassification handled as smuggling.

The practical defence is to classify the way customs does: from the tariff text and notes, checked against published rulings, with the product's composition, function and use documented — not from a supplier's guess or a database keyword search.

## Advance rulings: making your code binding before you ship

An advance ruling is a written decision customs issues to an applicant before goods are imported or exported, settling how a defined customs matter will be treated, and it converts your biggest classification unknowns into a binding answer. The governing rules are GACC Order No. 236 (the Provisional Measures on Advance Ruling Administration) and Announcement No. 14 of 2018, and the mechanics are concrete ([GACC advance ruling conditions, Lanzhou Customs](http://lanzhou.customs.gov.cn/lanzhou_customs/553151/553153/553155/4831009/2025121615203059388.docx)):

- **What it covers.** Three matters: commodity classification; origin or origin qualification; and dutiable-price-related elements and valuation methods — royalties, commissions, freight and insurance, and the effect of a special relationship.
- **Who applies.** A foreign trade operator registered with China customs and actually involved in the trade — the import consignee or export consignor, or their agent. A foreign brand without a China-registered operator applies through its importer of record.
- **When.** At least **three months** before the planned import, filed with the customs directly under GACC where the applicant is registered. One application covers one customs matter.
- **How fast.** Customs decides whether to accept within **10 days** and issues the ruling within **60 days** of acceptance.
- **How long it lasts.** The ruling is valid for **three years**, binding on customs for identical goods while it lasts; a renewal filed 30 to 90 days before expiry produces a fresh three-year ruling ([renewal rules, Announcement No. 32 of 2024, Wuhan Customs](http://wuhan.customs.gov.cn/gongbei_customs/2025-05/30/article_2026063015094263532.html)).

The application itself is a classification exercise: you must submit the order or letter of intent, product images and detailed technical data — composition, materials, production process, structure, function, principle, use, specifications — with Chinese translations. That is also why the ruling is valuable: it forces a defensible file to exist before the first declaration.

## Administrative rulings and classification decisions: the answers already in force

Beyond applicant-specific rulings, GACC publishes two instruments with nationwide force, and checking them is part of any competent classification file. A **classification decision** is GACC's own universally binding determination for defined goods: once published, identical goods must be classified the same way everywhere, and the decision stands until GACC modifies or revokes it, with publication of any change ([Provisions, Arts. 21–24](https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2021-10/29/content_5647589.htm)). An **administrative ruling** answers a general classification question raised through the prescribed procedure and binds customs nationwide from publication.

The distinction matters when you inherit a product line or benchmark a distributor's history. If a classification decision covers your goods, the conversation with customs is over — your file simply cites it. If published advance rulings cover similar products, they show how customs reasoned about the same materials and functions, which is the closest thing China customs offers to a searchable casebook. GACC's own policy-briefing channel regularly walks importers through these determinations, including how a heading's text, notes and GRI sequence combine to place a product ([GACC Customs Policy Direct briefing on classification and valuation, July 2026](http://www.customs.gov.cn/customs/2026-07/30/article_2026073010485045874.html)).

The table summarises the three instruments side by side:

<div class="table-wrap"><table>
<thead><tr><th>Instrument</th><th>Who it covers</th><th>How to get it</th><th>Effect and duration</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td>Advance ruling (Order No. 236)</td><td>The named applicant's own shipments</td><td>Apply 3 months before import to your registered customs; 10-day acceptance, 60-day issue</td><td>Binding 3 years; renewable for 3 more</td></tr>
<tr><td>Classification decision (Order No. 252)</td><td>All identical goods, nationwide</td><td>Issued by GACC on its own initiative and published</td><td>Universally binding until modified or revoked</td></tr>
<tr><td>Administrative ruling (Order No. 252)</td><td>Anyone importing goods within its scope</td><td>Issued by GACC through the prescribed ruling procedure and published</td><td>Binds customs nationwide from publication</td></tr>
</tbody></table></div>

## How GOODSINFINITE settles classification before your first shipment

We treat the code as an entry-stage deliverable, not a customs-house formality. As the Hong Kong importer of record working with bonded capacity in Tianjin, Shanghai, Ningbo, Guangzhou and Qingdao, we build the classification file — tariff text, notes, GRI sequence, published decisions — before quoting a landed cost, and we prepare advance-ruling applications for products where the duty, tax or licence outcome is genuinely contested. Because we price [landed cost](https://www.goods-infinite.com/insights/china-import-taxes-landed-cost.html) and [customs clearance](https://www.goods-infinite.com/insights/china-customs-clearance-process.html) on the same code customs will audit against, the rate we quote and the rate you pay are the same number. Our [China market entry guide](https://www.goods-infinite.com/guide-china-market-entry.html) places classification inside the five-stage entry sequence, and the [glossary](https://www.goods-infinite.com/glossary.html) defines the terms used here.

## FAQ

**How is the HS code for goods imported into China determined?** Under the Harmonized System convention using China's Import Tariff as the base, applying the six General Rules of Interpretation, the section and chapter notes, the subheading notes and national subheading notes, plus any published administrative rulings and classification decisions. Classification follows the actual state of the goods at declaration; for advance declarations, their actual state on arrival at the customs supervision zone.

**What happens if I use the wrong HS code for China imports?** The code drives duty, consumption tax, licences and inspection flags, so an error moves all of them at once. Customs re-assesses or refunds duty, charges late-payment surcharges, and can penalise misdeclaration up to three times the evaded duty — deliberate misclassification is handled as smuggling.

**How do I get a binding HS classification decision from China customs?** File an advance ruling application at least three months before the planned import with the customs directly under GACC where you are registered; customs decides on acceptance within 10 days and issues the ruling within 60 days. The ruling binds for three years and can be renewed for a further three.

**Who can apply for a China customs advance ruling?** A foreign trade operator registered with China customs and actually involved in the trade — the import consignee or export consignor, or their agent. Foreign brands without a China-registered operator apply through their importer of record; one application covers one customs matter, with full technical documentation and Chinese translations.

**What is the difference between an advance ruling, an administrative ruling and a classification decision?** An advance ruling binds for a specific applicant for three years. An administrative ruling answers a general question and binds customs nationwide from publication. A classification decision is GACC's universally binding determination for defined goods — identical goods must be classified the same way everywhere, until GACC modifies or revokes it.

## Double 11 and 618 for Foreign Brands: A Campaign Calendar for Cross-Border Stores
Source: https://www.goods-infinite.com/insights/double-11-618-campaign-calendar-foreign-brands
Published: 2026-09-14 · Cluster: E-commerce Operations

## Double 11 and 618 are the two demand peaks that decide a cross-border store's year

Double 11 and 618 are China's two recurring, platform-wide shopping festivals, and for a foreign brand running a cross-border store they function as the year's two demand peaks around which inventory, cash flow and marketing budgets should be planned. Double 11 — the 11 November festival that began as Singles' Day — is the larger of the two; 618, which grew out of JD.com's June anniversary sale, is the mid-year counterpart. Together they no longer resemble discount days at all: each now spans roughly four to six weeks, and third-party data show the gap between them narrowing. Syntun estimated total GMV across major platforms at RMB 1.695 trillion for Double 11 2025, up 14.2 percent year on year, and RMB 855.6 billion for 618 2025, up 15.2 percent. A brand that plans around these two windows — and around the supply-chain lead times they impose — competes on different terms from one that treats them as optional promotions.

<div class="statcard"><span class="n">RMB 1.695T</span><span class="l">Estimated total GMV across Chinese e-commerce platforms during Double 11 2025, up 14.2 percent year on year — with 618 2025 adding a further RMB 855.6 billion four months earlier</span><span class="src">Source: Syntun retail monitoring, via Dao Insights and Reuters, November 2025 / June 2025</span></div>

## Double 11 is now a six-week season, not a single day

Double 11 is China's largest annual online shopping festival, held around 11 November but now opened in waves that start in mid-October, and the shape of the event has changed more than its size. In 2025, Tmall opened its first sales wave on the evening of 20 October; in the first hour alone, 80 brands each passed RMB 100 million in GMV, more than 30,500 brands doubled their first-hour sales versus the prior year, and nearly 19,000 brands' first-hour sales exceeded their entire 2024 festival. Kuaishou began even earlier, on 7 October. The consequence for a foreign brand is that the "day" customers actually wait for is the first wave — by the second and third waves, much of the demand has already been banked.

Cross-border participation is no longer marginal. Tmall Global reported more than 1,700 overseas brands from 43 countries and regions entering the 2025 festival, led by new arrivals from the United States, South Korea, Australia, Japan and New Zealand — and across the first three quarters of 2025 the platform added 1,724 overseas brand first-stores, about seven per day, with South Korean brand numbers up more than 40 percent year on year. The festival has also become the year's clearest demand signal: categories such as oral anti-ageing supplements and ingredient-led skincare were the ones overseas brands pushed hardest into the event.

## 618 is the mid-year test run that brands should not skip

618 is China's largest mid-year shopping festival, centred on 18 June but running from mid-May, and it matters to foreign brands for two reasons beyond its own GMV. First, it is a genuine demand event in its own right: in 2025, pre-sales began on 13 May — a week earlier than 2024 — and the festival produced a record RMB 855.6 billion in GMV, with Tmall ranked first, followed by JD.com, Douyin and Pinduoduo. Four hundred and fifty-three brands each exceeded RMB 100 million on Taobao and Tmall, and category data from Syntun show imported-relevant segments performing strongly: skincare at RMB 43.2 billion, perfume and colour cosmetics at RMB 14.3 billion, nutrition and health supplements at RMB 14.3 billion, and pet food at RMB 7.5 billion during the festival window.

Second, and less obviously, 618 is where the demand pattern that will repeat in November gets rehearsed. The mechanisms tested at 618 — platforms cancelling complex coupon stacking in favour of simple "official direct discounts", government consumption subsidies folded into category pricing, and content platforms such as Xiaohongshu and Bilibili integrated into the conversion path — are the ones that carry into Double 11. A brand that treats 618 as a quiet period forfeits both the revenue and the learning.

## Preparation is a working-backwards exercise from the first sales wave

Campaign preparation for a cross-border store is a supply-chain scheduling exercise in which every task is anchored to the date the first sales wave opens, not to the festival's calendar peak. The binding constraint is inbound logistics: goods must physically arrive in a bonded warehouse and be ready for sale before the first wave, and cross-border import volume peaks in the weeks before both festivals, when customs and quarantine capacity is at its tightest. The timeline below reflects how a 1210 bonded-model store builds toward a mid-October first wave for Double 11 — the same structure applies to 618, shifted to a mid-May first wave.

<div class="table-wrap"><table><thead><tr><th>Timing</th><th>Workstream</th><th>What must be done</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>July–August (T-3 months)</td><td>Inventory and contracts</td><td>Forecast first-wave demand, place purchase orders, reserve bonded-warehouse space in the target city (Shanghai, Ningbo, Guangzhou, Qingdao or Tianjin), confirm the TP or agency's festival staffing</td></tr>
<tr><td>September (T-6 weeks)</td><td>Inbound shipping</td><td>Ship goods so bonded-stock arrival and entry are confirmed by late September; file product information, labels and positive-list compliance checks</td></tr>
<tr><td>Mid-September (T-5 weeks)</td><td>Platform submission</td><td>Submit campaign pricing, wave-by-wave discount structure, stock allocation and livestream slot requests to the platform</td></tr>
<tr><td>Early October (T-3 weeks)</td><td>Content seeding</td><td>Begin KOL and Xiaohongshu seeding, since conversion advertising before seeding warms no audience; brief livestream operators on the first-wave script</td></tr>
<tr><td>20 October (first wave)</td><td>Peak operations</td><td>Live customer service, real-time bonded-stock monitoring, same-day order pushes to warehouse teams; second and third waves through 11 November</td></tr>
</tbody></table></div>

The single most common calendar failure is in the September row: bonded stock that has not arrived, or has arrived but not completed entry procedures, by early October. There is no recovery from that inside the festival — the demand simply goes to competitors whose shelves are stocked.

## A 1210 cross-border store has four festival rules domestic stores never face

A 1210 bonded-model store operates under cross-border e-commerce retail import rules that change how festival demand can be captured, and foreign brands should plan around four of them specifically. First, inventory must be pre-positioned: goods arrive in bulk in a bonded warehouse before sale, and festival readiness is measured by confirmed bonded stock, not by factory capacity. Second, products must sit on the cross-border retail import positive list — the 2022 revision covers 1,476 tariff lines — so a category check belongs in the July planning step, not in October. Third, order sizes are capped: RMB 5,000 per single order and RMB 26,000 per buyer per year, with duty at zero and VAT and consumption tax charged at 70 percent of statutory rates inside those limits — an effective 9.1 percent tax for a typical 13 percent VAT good, per GACC's cross-border tax guidance. Fourth, goods are personal-use imports that cannot be resold onward, which means festival volume converts directly to end-customer orders rather than to distributor pipelines.

None of these rules is a barrier; each is a planning input. The tax advantage inside the caps is in fact one reason imported goods price competitively during festivals — but only for stores whose bonded stock, listing data and label compliance are all confirmed before the first wave opens ([GACC cross-border e-commerce retail import tax Q&A, January 2026](http://www.customs.gov.cn/customs/2026-01/13/article_2026041015241877353.html)).

## Budget for a season, and let content lead conversion

Festival budgeting for a foreign brand is the allocation of spend across a six-week season — content seeding first, conversion advertising second — rather than a bid for one discount day, and the platforms' own 2025 mechanics reward that order. The industry shift toward simple, transparent pricing ("official direct discounts" replacing coupon stacking) means a brand's campaign price must be defensible across the whole window, because consumers now compare across waves and across platforms with less friction than before. Retention mechanics also grew in importance: membership programmes such as Tmall's 88VIP featured heavily in 2025, and repeat purchasers convert at materially lower acquisition cost in the second and third waves.

The practical allocation that works for first-time festival brands: lock prices early and keep them stable across waves; spend four to six weeks before the first wave on KOL, Xiaohongshu and short-video seeding; concentrate paid traffic and livestream budget in the first-wave window when intent peaks; and hold a reserve for the 11 November climax, where residual demand still concentrates. Brands that invert this — heavy ad spend, no seeding, prices that drift between waves — typically pay more for the same GMV.

## First-timers fail in the same three places every year

First-year festival failures for foreign brands cluster into three recognisable patterns, and each is avoidable at the planning stage. The first is stock arriving late — the September inbound deadline missed because purchase orders were placed against the calendar date of 11 November rather than the mid-October first wave. The second is pricing built for a single day: a discount so deep it erases margin for six weeks, or a price that changes between waves and triggers platform and consumer distrust. The third is treating content as an afterthought — launching conversion advertising into a cold audience in late October, then concluding that "Double 11 doesn't work for our category" when the store simply had no warmed demand to convert.

The pattern behind all three is the same: the festival is a supply-chain and content event that ends in a sales spike, not a sales event with a supply chain attached. Brands that anchor every workstream to the first-wave date — stock confirmed, prices locked, audience warmed — enter November with the only three assets that festival demand can actually convert.

## China Import Taxes and Duties Explained: A Landed-Cost Walkthrough for Foreign Brands
Source: https://www.goods-infinite.com/insights/china-import-taxes-landed-cost
Published: 2026-09-11 · Cluster: Logistics & Distribution

## China import tax is three charges, not one

China import tax is the combined customs duty, import VAT and consumption tax levied on goods entering the country, calculated on a customs dutiable value rather than on the price you sell at. Most foreign brands treat it as a single rate they can look up, and that is where landed-cost models go wrong: the three charges have different bases and different recovery rules, and your import route swaps one set of rules for another. Get the structure right and landed cost becomes predictable to within a few percent, which is what makes pricing and distributor margins defensible.

<div class="statcard"><span class="n">9.1%</span><span class="l">All-in tax on a typical cross-border e-commerce (1210) import below the limits — zero duty plus import VAT charged at 70 percent of the statutory amount — against duty, consumption tax and full import VAT on the same goods cleared under general trade</span><span class="src">Source: GACC cross-border e-commerce tax policy Q&A, January 2026 (applying 财关税〔2016〕18号 and 财关税〔2018〕49号)</span></div>

## How customs duty is calculated: the dutiable value and the tariff rate

Customs duty in China is an ad valorem charge calculated as the dutiable value of the shipment multiplied by the tariff rate for that HS line and country of origin. The dutiable value is a CIF figure — transaction price plus international freight and insurance up to the port or bonded zone of entry — so freight sits inside the tax base, not on top of it.

Which rate applies is decided by origin and classification:

- **MFN rate** — the default for WTO members, and the ceiling to model against.
- **Provisional rate** — below-MFN, applied to 935 tariff lines in 2026, mainly key components, advanced materials and certain medical products; withdrawn for micro motors, printing machines and sulphuric acid, which returned to MFN ([GACC interpretation of the 2026 Tariff Adjustment Plan, effective 1 January 2026](http://www.customs.gov.cn/customs/2025-12/31/article_2025123119401553789.html)).
- **Agreement rate** — preferential rates under the 24 free-trade agreements China has in force with 34 trading partners, which can take a line to zero.
- **Special preferential rate** — zero tariff on all lines from the 43 least-developed countries with which China has diplomatic relations.

The 2026 plan brings the tariff schedule to 8,972 lines. Duty below RMB 50 on a single consignment is waived, so samples often clear duty-free ([GACC tariff administration guidance](http://shenyang.customs.gov.cn/eportal/ui?pageId=434597&msgDataId=5c427e87453949c0a2016ddf059a6966)); and because the rate follows the HS line, classification is a pricing decision as much as a compliance one.

## Import VAT is the largest line — and usually recoverable

Import VAT is the value-added tax charged at the border on the composite assessable value — CIF plus duty plus consumption tax — at either 13 percent or 9 percent under China's VAT Law, in force since 1 January 2026.

**Import VAT = (CIF + customs duty + consumption tax) × VAT rate**

Thirteen percent is the default for goods and imports. Nine percent is a closed list: agricultural products, edible vegetable oils and edible salt, water, heating, coal gas and natural gas, books, newspapers and periodicals, and feed, fertiliser, pesticide, agricultural machinery and agricultural film ([STA, VAT Law rate schedule in force from 1 January 2026](https://hunan.chinatax.gov.cn/show/20260211055577)). Food and beverage brands should check which list their line falls into first.

The rate matters less than the recovery rule. Import VAT is creditable input tax for a general taxpayer in China, so a mainland importer deducts it against the VAT it collects on domestic sales. That makes the genuinely unrecoverable cost of a general-trade import **duty plus consumption tax** — the distinction most brands miss when benchmarking a distributor's quote, and the reason a distributor can work on a thinner margin than the border tax figure suggests.

## Consumption tax applies to 15 categories only

Consumption tax in China is a single-stage excise levied at importation and manufacture on 15 defined categories of goods, and it is charged outside the tax base — which is why the formula divides rather than multiplies. It applies to unit values, not brands, and is never creditable.

**Consumption tax (ad valorem) = (CIF + customs duty) ÷ (1 − rate) × rate**

Most consumer goods carry none: apparel, homeware, toys, electronics and most skincare sit outside the list. The categories that bite for imported consumer brands are narrow but sharp ([STA consumption tax rate schedule](https://xinjiang.chinatax.gov.cn/xwdt/ztzl/xwqy/rdjd/202306/t20230620_116721.htm)):

- **High-end cosmetics — 15 percent**, applied when the dutiable unit value reaches RMB 10 per millilitre or gram, or RMB 15 per piece, excluding VAT. A cream below the threshold pays nothing; priced above it, the whole value is taxed.
- **Alcohol — wine 10 percent**, spirits 20 percent plus RMB 0.5 per 500 ml, rice wine RMB 240 per tonne, beer RMB 220 to 250 per tonne.
- **High-end watches 20 percent**; jewellery 5 percent for gold and diamonds, 10 percent for other precious stones; passenger cars 1 to 40 percent by engine size, plus an extra rate on ultra-luxury models; golf equipment and yachts 10 percent.

## Cross-border e-commerce tax: the simplified regime behind the 1210 model

Cross-border e-commerce retail import tax is a separate, simplified regime for 1210 bonded and 9610 direct-mail orders, in which customs duty is temporarily set at zero and import VAT and consumption tax are charged at 70 percent of the statutory amount. It exists for personal-use imports, not commercial trade, and it is the single largest tax difference available to a foreign brand entering China.

The mechanics come from two notices — 财关税〔2016〕18号 and 财关税〔2018〕49号 — applied by customs as follows ([GACC cross-border e-commerce tax policy Q&A, January 2026](http://www.customs.gov.cn/customs/2026-01/13/article_2026041015241877353.html)):

- The single-transaction limit is **RMB 5,000**; the annual limit per individual is **RMB 26,000**.
- Within the limits, duty is 0 percent and VAT and consumption tax are charged at 70 percent of the statutory amount — an effective 9.1 percent for a 13 percent VAT good, or RMB 9.1 of tax on a RMB 100 order.
- The dutiable value is the **actual transaction price**, including retail price, freight and insurance.
- An order above RMB 5,000 but under the annual limit containing one item may still use the channel, at full goods rates and counted against the annual total; beyond it, shipments are managed as general trade.

A published worked example shows the interaction. An eye cream at RMB 425 for 20 g has a dutiable unit value of RMB 21.25 per gram, above the RMB 10 threshold, so 15 percent consumption tax applies: 425 ÷ (1 − 15%) × 15% = RMB 75, charged at 70 percent = RMB 52.50. VAT is computed on the full consumption tax figure, also at 70 percent: (425 + 75) × 13% × 70% = RMB 45.50. Total tax is RMB 98, or 23.1 percent of the consumer's price ([Ningbo Customs guidance, November 2025](http://wuhan.customs.gov.cn/hhht_customs/566254/cjsfw/kjdswgbsjkyw/xfz/index.html)).

The catch is structural: cross-border goods are for personal use and **cannot be resold**, and every order consumes part of the buyer's RMB 26,000 quota. That eventually forces a successful brand onto general trade — model the tax gap as a scaling cost, not a permanent advantage.

## Same product, two routes: the landed-cost arithmetic side by side

A landed-cost model for China is the build-up of every charge from ex-works price to a unit in domestic stock — duty, import VAT, consumption tax, freight, bonded storage and platform fees — and your import route reroutes the first three. The table runs the same high-end cosmetic, a 15 percent consumption-tax product, through both regimes: general trade on a CIF value of RMB 300 with an illustrative 6 percent MFN duty rate, and cross-border on the consumer's actual transaction price of RMB 500, which is the dutiable value in that regime.

<div class="table-wrap"><table>
<thead><tr><th>Landed cost line</th><th>General trade (0110)</th><th>Cross-border 1210 / 9610</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td>Tax base</td><td>CIF RMB 300 (goods + freight + insurance)</td><td>Transaction price RMB 500 (retail + freight + insurance)</td></tr>
<tr><td>Customs duty</td><td>RMB 18.00 (6% of CIF)</td><td>RMB 0.00 (0% within limits)</td></tr>
<tr><td>Consumption tax (15%)</td><td>RMB 56.12</td><td>RMB 61.76 (RMB 88.24 at 70%)</td></tr>
<tr><td>Import VAT (13%)</td><td>RMB 48.64</td><td>RMB 53.53 (at 70%)</td></tr>
<tr><td>Total tax</td><td>RMB 122.76 — 40.9% of CIF</td><td>RMB 115.29 — 23.1% of retail price</td></tr>
<tr><td>Recoverable?</td><td>VAT creditable for a general taxpayer; duty and consumption tax are not</td><td>Not recoverable — tax is collected per order</td></tr>
<tr><td>Resale</td><td>Full commercial sale and distribution</td><td>Personal use only — no resale</td></tr>
</tbody></table></div>

The lesson is not simply that cross-border is cheaper. On general trade, RMB 74.12 of the RMB 122.76 bill is unrecoverable duty and consumption tax; the cross-border consumer pays 23.1 percent on a higher base. Cross-border wins on speed and cash flow, general trade on scale, once volume can absorb duty and excise. For the surrounding unit economics, see our [1210 bonded import guide](https://www.goods-infinite.com/insights/what-is-1210-bonded-import.html) and our [transparent import pricing explainer](https://www.goods-infinite.com/insights/transparent-import-pricing.html).

## Five variables that move your China landed cost

A China landed-cost model is only as accurate as its inputs, and five of them move the answer materially.

1. **HS classification.** Duty and consumption tax are line-level facts, not brand-level ones; one error can shift duty by ten percentage points or pull a product into the excise list. See our [customs clearance walkthrough](https://www.goods-infinite.com/insights/china-customs-clearance-process.html).
2. **Country of origin.** FTA origin can take duty to zero, and an origin attracting retaliatory duty does the opposite — origin follows manufacturing location, not paperwork.
3. **Route.** General trade, 1210 bonded and 9610 direct mail carry three different treatments, and the right answer changes as volume grows.
4. **Consumption-tax status.** Check unit-value thresholds before setting shelf price: RMB 11 per millilitre instead of RMB 9.5 costs 15 percent on the entire value.
5. **What sits inside the dutiable value — and whether the VAT is creditable.** Freight, insurance and certain royalties are in the tax base; and on general trade through a mainland importer the import VAT is recoverable, while on cross-border retail it never is. Two models with identical headline rates can differ by more than 10 percent of unit cost on this alone.

Our [China market entry guide](https://www.goods-infinite.com/guide-china-market-entry.html) places tax modelling inside the wider five-stage entry sequence, and the [glossary](https://www.goods-infinite.com/glossary.html) defines the customs terms used here.

## How GOODSINFINITE models tax for brand clients

We run the landed-cost model before recommending a route, not after. As the Hong Kong importer of record with bonded capacity in Tianjin, Shanghai, Ningbo, Guangzhou and Qingdao, we price the same product through the 1210, 9610 and general-trade routes side by side and show which carries the lowest non-recoverable cost at your forecast volume. Duty, import VAT, consumption tax, bonded storage and domestic delivery stay on separate lines, never bundled into one "all-in" rate.

## FAQ

**How much tax do you pay to import goods into China?** It depends on the route, not just the product. On general trade you pay customs duty on the CIF value, consumption tax on the 15 excise categories, and import VAT at 13 percent or 9 percent on the composite value of CIF plus duty plus consumption tax. On cross-border e-commerce retail within the RMB 5,000 single-order and RMB 26,000 annual limits, duty is set at zero and VAT and consumption tax are charged at 70 percent of the statutory amount — an effective 9.1 percent for most goods.

**What is the difference between China import duty and import VAT?** Import duty is a customs charge on the dutiable value (CIF) multiplied by the tariff rate for your HS line and country of origin, and it is never recoverable. Import VAT is charged on the composite assessable value and is creditable input tax for a general VAT taxpayer in China, so the genuinely non-recoverable cost on general trade is duty plus consumption tax.

**Which imported products pay consumption tax in China?** Only 15 categories. High-end cosmetics is the one that most often surprises beauty brands: 15 percent when the dutiable unit value reaches RMB 10 per millilitre or gram, or RMB 15 per piece, excluding VAT. The other common categories are alcohol, high-end watches, jewellery, passenger cars by engine size, golf equipment and yachts.

**Why is the tax on cross-border e-commerce so much lower than general trade?** Because it is a deliberately simplified regime for personal-use imports below the limits, not a commercial one: duty is temporarily zero and VAT and consumption tax are charged at 70 percent of the statutory amount. The trade-off is that cross-border goods cannot be resold and each order consumes part of the buyer's RMB 26,000 annual quota, which caps volume.

**Does the freight cost affect China import tax?** Yes. China's customs dutiable value is a CIF value — transaction price plus international freight and insurance up to the port or bonded zone of entry — so freight sits inside the tax base. That is one reason high air-freight shipments carry a higher tax figure, and why sea freight or bonded consolidation can lower the total even when the goods cost the same.

## China Market Entry Roadmap for Fashion & Apparel Brands: Channels, Compliance and Timing
Source: https://www.goods-infinite.com/insights/china-market-entry-roadmap-fashion-apparel
Published: 2026-09-09 · Cluster: Market Research

## Why fashion and apparel need their own China market entry roadmap

A China market entry roadmap for fashion and apparel brands is a staged launch plan for clothing collections in mainland China, sequenced around two decisions most consumer categories never have to make: which import channel sets your retail price, and which mandatory safety standards your garment must meet before the first piece sells. A skincare brand waits on NMPA registration and a pet-food brand on MARA certificates, but clothing carries no pre-market registration at all — so the fashion timeline is compressed, and the mistakes that hurt fashion entrants are different ones: pricing on the wrong channel, garments that fail a border safety test, and labels filed too late. Generic entry advice misleads fashion brands exactly where the money is lost.

<div class="statcard"><span class="n">¥1.07T</span><span class="l">Retail sales of clothing by China's above-designated-size retailers in 2024 — with online clothing sales still growing (+1.5%)</span><span class="src">Source: National Bureau of Statistics data compiled in the China National Garment Association (CNGA) 2024 industry briefing</span></div>

## The China apparel market rewards brands that segment by price, not by size

Market segmentation in China's apparel industry is the price-tier structure — mass, premium and luxury — through which imported brands actually compete, and it is the first screen a fashion entrant should apply rather than category or size. China's above-designated-size retailers sold RMB 1.07 trillion of clothing in 2024 ([CNGA industry briefing, NBS data](https://www.cnga.org.cn)), a market that has matured: above-limit clothing retail grew only 0.1 percent in 2024 while online clothing sales rose 1.5 percent ([NBS 2024 retail data](https://www.stats.gov.cn)). Three structural facts matter more than the headline number:

- **The market has split into a premium lane and a value lane.** Mass-market competition is brutal on price, while premium and luxury tiers keep rewarding brand equity, materials and cut — the assets Western brands arrive with.
- **Discovery is online and visual first.** Young buyers form preference on Xiaohongshu and Douyin before they open Tmall or JD, so a fashion entrant's first marketing dollar goes to content seeding, not to media that announces a brand they have never heard of.
- **Imported labels hold a credible premium slot** — foreign brand perception is strongest precisely in the price tier where Chinese consumers expect design authority, and weakest in the mass lane dominated by domestic supply chains.

For an EU or US brand the strategic read is simple: do not compete in the mass lane. Compete where a 200-euro jacket still reads as a considered purchase, and validate that tier with the demand-research method described in our [China market research guide](https://www.goods-infinite.com/insights/china-market-research-foreign-brands.html) before committing inventory.

## Two import routes set the price: cross-border e-commerce or general trade

An import route for fashion is the customs mechanism through which garments enter China — cross-border e-commerce retail (1210 bonded or 9610 direct) or general trade — and each produces a different landed price, a different channel and a different speed to market. The cross-border route is the one most first-time fashion brands should start on: clothing, footwear and hats are on the cross-border retail import "positive list", which after the 2022 revision covers 1,476 tariff lines ([MOFCOM / Ministry of Finance positive list](https://gss.mof.gov.cn/gzdt/zhengcefabu/201912/t20191227_3451448.htm); [GACC policy Q&A, January 2026](http://www.customs.gov.cn/customs/2026-01/13/article_2026041015241877353.html)). Within the RMB 5,000 single-order and RMB 26,000 annual cap per buyer, goods are charged zero import duty and VAT and consumption tax at 70 percent of the statutory rate ([GACC consumer guidance, 1210 model](http://gongbei.customs.gov.cn/hhht_customs/566254/cjsfw/kjdswgbsjkyw/xfz/index.html)) — for apparel that means an effective tax bill of roughly 9.1 percent instead of the 20-plus percent a general-trade shipment commonly pays. Two further rules matter: the goods must be for personal use and cannot be resold, and the brand sells through platform flagships while a licensed import agent of record handles the bonded warehousing — the structure described in our [1210 guide](https://www.goods-infinite.com/insights/what-is-1210-bonded-import.html) and [Tmall Global setup guide](https://www.goods-infinite.com/insights/tmall-global-store-setup.html).

<div class="table-wrap"><table>
<thead><tr><th>Decision</th><th>Cross-border e-commerce (1210)</th><th>General trade</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td>Tax on a typical garment</td><td>0% duty within limits; VAT ≈ 9.1% (70% of 13%)</td><td>MFN duty ≈ 6–10% (some lines to 16%) + 13% VAT</td></tr>
<tr><td>China entity needed</td><td>No — overseas brand owner + import agent</td><td>Licensed importer of record; WFOE useful at scale</td></tr>
<tr><td>Channels</td><td>Tmall Global, JD Worldwide, Douyin cross-border</td><td>Wholesale, offline retail, marketplace domestic stores</td></tr>
<tr><td>Use constraint</td><td>Personal use only — no resale</td><td>Full commercial sale and distribution</td></tr>
<tr><td>Time to first sale</td><td>≈ 3–4 months</td><td>≈ 4–6 months</td></tr>
</tbody></table></div>

General trade becomes the right route once you need offline retail, wholesale distribution or full control of the domestic market — but it should be entered after the cross-border channel has validated demand, not before. Our [transparent import pricing guide](https://www.goods-infinite.com/insights/transparent-import-pricing.html) shows how to model the landed-cost difference on an actual collection.

## Standards and labelling are the fashion compliance gate — not registration

Fashion compliance in China is a product-safety and labelling regime — mandatory national standards GB 18401-2010 for textiles and GB 31701-2015 for infant and children's clothing, enforced by customs and market regulators at and after the border — rather than the pre-market registration that food, cosmetics and medical devices require. There is no CCC certificate and no approval to wait for; the gate is whether the finished garment passes the standard. GB 18401-2010 sets the basic safety requirements for textile products — pH limits (4.0–8.5), formaldehyde, prohibited dyes and colour-fastness minimums — while GB 31701-2015 (in force since June 2016) adds stricter rules for children's wear on cords, small parts and attachment strength ([SAMR mandatory standards platform](https://openstd.samr.gov.cn/bzgk/gb/)). Enforcement is real and recent: in its 2024 imported-consumer-goods inspection results, Beijing Customs reported that imported Italian trousers failed GB 18401 on water colour fastness and were destroyed, a Japanese T-shirt was returned for out-of-range pH, and a Korean baby romper was destroyed for neck cords breaching GB 31701 ([Beijing Customs 2024 cases](https://www.workercn.cn/c/2025-03-17/8479988.shtml)).

Two operational details keep a compliant brand out of that list. First, test to the Chinese standard before shipping — EU and US garment specs do not automatically satisfy GB 18401. Second, since December 2022 GACC has accepted third-party inspection reports under its commodity-inspection acceptance measures, with imported apparel named as the first eligible category — but of the 118 accepted laboratories only three sit outside mainland China (two in Hong Kong, China and one in Spain), so in practice plan for a test in a Chinese laboratory ([European Commission trade barrier note on China textile testing](https://trade.ec.europa.eu/access-to-markets/en/results?text=10303)). Our [Chinese labelling guide](https://www.goods-infinite.com/insights/china-import-product-labelling-requirements.html) covers the label build that must accompany the test.

## A realistic fashion timeline: 3–6 months from decision to first order

A realistic China entry timeline for a fashion brand is three to six months, because apparel needs no product registration — the calendar is set by trademark, testing, sizing and platform onboarding rather than by government approvals. The sequence that protects the calendar:

- **Month 1 — trademark and standards audit.** China is first-to-file, so register the Latin and Chinese marks before any factory, agent or platform conversation (see our [China trademark guide](https://www.goods-infinite.com/insights/china-trademark-registration-foreign-brand.html)), and send representative finished samples — fabric, trims, dyes — for a GB 18401 / GB 31701 test in a Chinese laboratory.
- **Month 1–2 — channel and pricing model.** Choose the 1210 cross-border route with a Tmall Global or JD Worldwide flagship, appoint a TP operator, and build the landed-cost model: FOB plus freight, the ~9.1 percent tax, bonded warehousing in Tianjin, Shanghai, Ningbo, Guangzhou or Qingdao, and platform fees.
- **Month 2–3 — size grading and Chinese label.** Regrade the collection to Chinese fit expectations and the GB/T 1335 sizing series where relevant — Asian-body sizing differs enough that EU sizes mislead — and commission the Chinese-language hang tag and care label against GB 18401/31701 content rules.
- **Month 3–4 — platform onboarding and first bonded shipment.** Complete Tmall Global onboarding with your TP, book the first container into the bonded warehouse, and soft-launch with a capsule collection.
- **Month 4–6 — seed and scale.** Start Xiaohongshu seeding and Douyin live-commerce tests once the store is live, read sell-through by style, then expand the collection — and only then evaluate general trade for offline and wholesale.

## Where imported fashion actually sells: flagship, seeding, live commerce, offline

The route-to-market for imported fashion in China is a channel sequence that opens with a cross-border flagship on Tmall Global or JD Worldwide, adds Xiaohongshu seeding and Douyin live commerce, and only later extends to general-trade offline distribution — and brands that respect the sequence convert demand before they commit to fixed retail costs. The flagship is the trust anchor where consumers verify the brand is official; Xiaohongshu is where fashion preference forms through outfit posts and honest reviews, making it the natural first stop for an apparel label ([Xiaohongshu marketing guide](https://www.goods-infinite.com/insights/xiaohongshu-red-marketing-foreign-brand.html)); Douyin adds volume through short-video and live commerce once the style resonates ([Douyin marketing guide](https://www.goods-infinite.com/insights/douyin-china-marketing-foreign-brand.html)). Offline, imported fashion matters in premium department stores and multi-brand boutiques, where the route runs through the distributor relationships described in our [China distributor guide](https://www.goods-infinite.com/insights/china-distributor-for-foreign-brands.html).

The principle underneath this roadmap is the same one that governs every category we cover: retire the cheap risks — trademark, standards, sizing — in month one, validate demand through the cross-border channel before spending on inventory or rent, and let sell-through, not the marketing plan, decide when to open the general-trade route. Our [China market entry guide](https://www.goods-infinite.com/guide-china-market-entry.html) places this roadmap inside the wider five-stage framework for foreign brands, and the [glossary](https://www.goods-infinite.com/glossary.html) explains the customs and platform terms used throughout.

## FAQ

**Does a foreign fashion brand need a China entity to start selling?** No. On the cross-border e-commerce route a foreign brand sells through platforms such as Tmall Global or JD Worldwide with its overseas entity as the brand owner, while a licensed import agent of record clears goods into the bonded warehouse — no WFOE is required. A China entity only becomes necessary later, when you move to general-trade wholesale or offline retail.

**Do imported clothes need product registration or CCC certification in China?** No. Apparel is not on China's CCC certification catalogue and needs no pre-market product registration, which is why fashion entry is far faster than food, cosmetics or medical devices. What gates your shipment instead is compliance with mandatory safety standards — GB 18401-2010 for general textiles and GB 31701-2015 for infant and children's clothing — plus correct Chinese-language labelling.

**How long does it take a fashion brand to start selling in China?** Plan for three to six months from decision to first sale — the fastest entry timeline of any major consumer category, because there is no registration to wait on. The work that takes time is done in parallel: China trademark filing, a GB 18401/GB 31701 compliance test, Chinese-label design, and platform onboarding with a Tmall Global partner (TP) operator.

**What duty and VAT apply to imported fashion and apparel?** On the cross-border e-commerce retail route, orders within the RMB 5,000 single-transaction and RMB 26,000 annual cap are charged zero import duty, with import VAT and consumption tax at 70 percent of the statutory rate — effectively about 9.1 percent VAT for apparel. On general trade, most finished clothing attracts an MFN duty of roughly 6 to 10 percent plus 13 percent import VAT, before free-trade-agreement reductions or additional US-origin retaliatory duties.

**What is the most common mistake foreign fashion brands make entering China?** Skipping the trademark filing and the standards test while the marketing plan is being built. China is first-to-file, so an unregistered Western label can be registered by a local trader before the brand arrives; and a garment that fails GB 18401 on pH, formaldehyde or colour fastness is stopped or destroyed at the border no matter how strong the brand is.
